summary.goal:
Build DELVE, a turn-based roguelike, in this repository: a deterministic game core in plain JavaScript (ES modules, Node 22+, no dependencies) with its own tests, and a 3D renderer for the browser built on three.js. Follow every rule below exactly; the core is driven by automated checks, and the rules below are the contract they check. Where the rules leave something open, decide, keep it consistent everywhere, and write it down.

# 1. Files and boundaries

- `package.json` exists (type module); add a "test" script so `npm test` runs every test with node:test. No dependencies of any kind, no build step.
- `src/` holds the core (pure JavaScript, no DOM, no timers, no randomness other than the seeded generator below) and the renderer. The core must run in Node; the renderer only in the browser.
- `index.html` at the root loads three.js from exactly this URL with a plain script tag: `https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/three.js/0.160.0/three.min.js` (the global `THREE`). Nothing else is loaded from the network. The page loads `src/main.js` as a module script with a relative path and must work from a file:// URL in Chrome started with `--allow-file-access-from-files` (the screenshot tool and the checks do that) or from any static file server; no build step, no bundler.
- Never use eval, new Function, node:vm, child_process, or dynamic code loading. The core modules (rng, map, fov, path, game) must not read the clock or Math.random; the page may use Math.random only to pick the seed of a new game.
- A custom tool named `screenshot` is available in this project: it opens an HTML file in headless Chrome, returns a screenshot and the page's console messages and errors. Use it whenever you change the page or the renderer; a page with console errors is not done.

# 2. Random numbers (`src/rng.js`)

`createRng(seed)` returns a generator implementing mulberry32 over the 32-bit unsigned seed `seed >>> 0`:

```
next(): state = (state + 0x6D2B79F5) >>> 0; t = state; t = Math.imul(t ^ (t >>> 15), t | 1); t ^= t + Math.imul(t ^ (t >>> 7), t | 61); return ((t ^ (t >>> 14)) >>> 0) / 4294967296;
```

`next()` returns a float in [0, 1); `int(max)` returns `Math.floor(next() * max)` (an integer in [0, max)); `pick(array)` returns `array[int(array.length)]`; `state` is readable and writable (the 32-bit unsigned number, always kept in that range), so a game can serialize it and restore it. For seed 123 the first three `next()` values are 0.7872516233474016, 0.1785435655619949, 0.49531551403924823.

# 3. Levels (`src/map.js`)

`generateLevel(seed, depth)` returns `{ width, height, tiles, rooms, start, stairs }`:

- `width` is 60 and `height` is 30. `tiles` is an array of `height` strings of `width` characters: `#` wall, `.` floor, `>` stairs down. Every tile on the outer border is a wall.
- Between 6 and 12 rooms: `rooms` is an array of `{ x, y, w, h }` describing rectangles of floor tiles (w and h between 3 and 10). Rooms never touch: for any two rooms there is at least one wall tile between them in every direction (the rectangles enlarged by one tile do not overlap). Rooms are connected by corridors of floor tiles.
- Every floor tile (and the stairs) is reachable from `start` by 8-directional movement over non-wall tiles.
- `start` is a floor tile inside the first room; `stairs` is a tile inside another room: the room whose centre `(x + w / 2, y + h / 2)` is farthest from `start` (Euclidean distance; the first such room in `rooms` on a tie). For depth below 5 the stairs tile is `>`; on depth 5 (the last one) there is no `>` anywhere and `stairs` is a plain floor tile where the Amulet lies.
- The same seed and depth always produce the identical level; generation uses only `createRng(seed)`.

Passable tiles are `.` and `>`. Everything else in this document that says "adjacent" or "step" means the 8 neighbouring tiles (Chebyshev distance 1), diagonals included, with no corner-cutting rule.

# 4. Field of view (`src/fov.js`)

`computeFov(tiles, x, y, radius)` returns a Set of strings `"x,y"` of the visible tiles, defined exactly like this: a tile T is visible from the origin O when its Euclidean distance satisfies dx*dx + dy*dy <= radius*radius and every tile on the Bresenham line from O to T, excluding T itself, is not a wall. The origin is always visible. Walls are visible when the line reaches them. The Bresenham line is the integer algorithm:

```
dx = |x1 - x0|; dy = -|y1 - y0|; sx = x0 < x1 ? 1 : -1; sy = y0 < y1 ? 1 : -1; err = dx + dy;
loop: visit (x0, y0); if (x0 == x1 && y0 == y1) stop; e2 = 2 * err; if (e2 >= dy) { err += dy; x0 += sx; } if (e2 <= dx) { err += dx; y0 += sy; }
```

# 5. Pathfinding (`src/path.js`)

`findPath(tiles, from, to, blocked = [])` returns the shortest path from `from` to `to` as an array of `{ x, y }` steps, excluding the start and including the target, moving 8-directionally over passable tiles; `blocked` is a list of `{ x, y }` tiles that count as impassable (except the target itself). It returns `null` when there is no path. Any shortest path is acceptable; its length must be minimal.

# 6. The game (`src/game.js`)

`createGame(options)` creates a game. `options.seed` (integer, default 1) seeds everything. Without a fixture the game generates depth 1 with `generateLevel(levelSeed(seed, 1), 1)` where `levelSeed(seed, depth) = (seed + depth * 7919) >>> 0`, places the player at `start`, and populates the level (section 8). With a fixture the level is exactly what the caller says: `options.map` is an array of row strings (any size, same characters), `options.player` is `{ x, y }`, `options.monsters` is an array of `{ type, x, y }`, `options.items` an array of `{ kind, x, y, amount? }`; a fixture level gets no generated monsters or items and no stairs unless the map contains `>`.

`game.state` is a plain, JSON-serialisable object with at least these fields (extra fields are allowed):

```
{ seed, depth, turn, status,             // status: "playing" | "dead" | "won"
  width, height, tiles,                   // tiles: array of row strings
  visible, explored,                      // visible: array of "x,y" strings; explored: array of row strings of "0"/"1"
  player: { x, y, hp, maxHp, attack, defense, level, xp, gold, inventory, equipment: { weapon, armor } },
  monsters: [ { id, type, x, y, hp, maxHp, attack, defense, xp } ],
  items: [ { id, kind, x, y, amount } ],  // amount only for gold
  log }                                   // array of strings, the most recent last, at most 50 kept
```

The player starts with hp 30, maxHp 30, attack 5, defense 1, level 1, xp 0, gold 0, an empty inventory and no equipment. `visible` is recomputed after every action with `computeFov` from the player's tile with radius 8; `explored` marks every tile that has ever been visible.

`game.act(action)` performs one player action; when the action costs a turn, `turn` increases by one and then every monster takes its turn (section 7). It returns the array of log messages the action produced. Actions:

- `{ type: "move", dx, dy }` with dx, dy in -1..1, not both 0. Into a passable tile with no monster: the player moves (costs a turn). Into a monster: the player attacks it (costs a turn). Into a wall or off the map: nothing happens, no turn, a message such as "There is a wall in the way."
- `{ type: "wait" }`: costs a turn.
- `{ type: "pickup" }`: picks up the items on the player's tile. Gold is never stored: it adds `amount` to `player.gold` (message "You pick up N gold."). The Amulet ends the game: status becomes "won", message "You found the Amulet of Yendor! You win." Every other item goes to the inventory as `{ kind, name }`, which holds at most 10 items; an item that does not fit stays on the floor with the message "Your pack is full." The action costs a turn when at least one item was picked up. With nothing on the tile: no turn, message "There is nothing here."
- `{ type: "use", index }`: uses inventory item `index` (0-based). A potion heals 10 hp, capped at maxHp, and is consumed. A weapon or armor is equipped into the matching slot; the item previously in that slot, if any, returns to the inventory. Costs a turn. An invalid index: no turn, a message.
- `{ type: "drop", index }`: moves the inventory item to the floor at the player's tile (costs a turn). Invalid index: no turn.
- `{ type: "descend" }`: only on a `>` tile; otherwise no turn and a message. On the stairs: depth increases by one, the new level is `generateLevel(levelSeed(seed, depth), depth)` populated per section 8, the player stands on its `start`, visible and explored start over, turn continues counting; the message is "You descend to depth N." It costs a turn, so the new level's monsters act once (none of them starts next to the player).

When status is not "playing", `act` changes nothing and returns [].

Combat is deterministic. The player's effective attack is `attack` plus the equipped weapon's bonus (dagger 1, sword 3); effective defense is `defense` plus the equipped armor's bonus (leather 1, chain 2). Damage dealt = max(1, attacker's effective attack - defender's effective defense). A monster whose hp reaches 0 or less is removed, the player gains its xp, message "You kill the <type>." (before that, "You hit the <type> for N."). A monster attacking the player: message "The <type> hits you for N."; when the player's hp reaches 0 or less, hp is 0, status becomes "dead", message "You die."

Levels: after gaining xp, while `xp >= threshold(level + 1)` with `threshold(L) = 5 * L * (L - 1)` (level 2 at 10 xp, level 3 at 30, level 4 at 60, level 5 at 100): level increases by one, maxHp increases by 5, hp increases by 5 (capped at the new maxHp), attack increases by 1, message "Welcome to level N."

`game.serialize()` returns a JSON string; `loadGame(json)` returns a game whose state and future behaviour are identical to the original (include the rng state). `game.hash()` returns a string: FNV-1a 32-bit hash, as 8 lowercase hex digits, of `JSON.stringify` of the state with every object's keys sorted recursively.

`applyKey(game, key)` maps one key to an action and performs it, returning the messages, or `null` for a key that is not an action: h j k l y u b n move (h left, l right, k up, j down, y up-left, u up-right, b down-left, n down-right; up means y - 1), `.` wait, `g` pickup, `>` descend, digits `1`..`9` use inventory item 0..8. `runScript(game, text)` applies the characters of `text` in order, skipping whitespace and unknown characters.

# 7. Monsters

| type | hp | attack | defense | xp | sight |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| rat | 4 | 2 | 0 | 3 | 5 |
| goblin | 8 | 3 | 1 | 6 | 6 |
| skeleton | 12 | 4 | 2 | 10 | 6 |
| orc | 18 | 6 | 2 | 15 | 7 |
| troll | 30 | 8 | 3 | 30 | 7 |

After each turn-costing player action, monsters act in increasing `id` order, one step or attack each. A monster adjacent to the player attacks. Otherwise, when the player's tile is in `computeFov` from the monster's tile with the monster's sight radius, it takes one step along `findPath` toward the player, treating other monsters as blocked; when no path exists it stays. Otherwise it wanders: with probability one half it stays, else it moves to a random adjacent passable tile that holds no monster and not the player, chosen with the game's rng. Monsters never share a tile with each other or with the player and never enter walls.

# 8. Populating a generated level

On a generated level of depth d: 3 + 2d monsters, each of a type chosen with the rng from the types allowed at that depth (depth 1: rat, goblin; depth 2: rat, goblin, skeleton; depth 3: goblin, skeleton, orc; depth 4: skeleton, orc; depth 5: orc, troll), placed on distinct floor tiles outside the first room. 3 + d items on distinct floor tiles that hold no monster and are not the player's tile: each item is a potion with probability 0.4, gold with 0.3 (amount = 5 + int(16) coins), else one of dagger, sword, leather, chain with equal probability. On depth 5 an additional item of kind "amulet" lies on the level's `stairs` tile. Item ids and monster ids are unique within the game.

# 9. The page and the renderer

`index.html` plus `src/main.js` (a module) and whatever renderer modules you like:

- URL parameters: `seed` (integer) fixes the seed; `script` is a key string applied with `runScript` before the first frame. When either parameter is present the title screen is skipped and the game starts at once; otherwise a title screen with the game's name and controls waits for any key and the seed is random.
- A HUD element with id `hud` whose text contains `HP 30/30`, `Depth 1` and `Turn 0` at the start of a new game (and the current values afterwards), the player's level, xp and gold. A message log element with id `log` showing the last messages. An inventory panel toggled with `i`, listing items by number.
- Keyboard: the keys of section 6, plus arrow keys for the four directions, `R` to restart after death or victory, `?` for help. Death and victory screens.
- The renderer is three.js: floor tiles, walls with height, the stairs, the player and each monster type as distinct low-poly meshes or coloured shapes with a glyph label, items as small shapes; unexplored tiles are not drawn, explored tiles outside the current view are dimmed, visible tiles are lit; a light follows the player; the camera looks down at the player from above and behind and follows smoothly; a hit flashes the target and shakes the screen briefly, a kill spawns a short particle burst; monsters and the player move with a short tween rather than teleporting. A dark palette with a few strong accent colours. Optional: WebAudio beeps for hits and pickups.
- Expose the game as `window.game` for debugging.

# 10. Tests and documentation

Every core module has node:test tests in `test/`; cover generation constraints, field of view, paths, combat numbers, items, levels, stairs, serialization and determinism (the same seed and script give the same hash). Write a README.md: how to play, the controls, the architecture (modules, the state shape, how the renderer reads the state), and how to run the tests. npm test must pass.

project.goal:
Build DELVE, a turn-based roguelike, in this repository: a deterministic game core in plain JavaScript (ES modules, Node 22+, no dependencies) with its own tests, and a 3D renderer for the browser built on three.js. Follow every rule below exactly; the core is driven by automated checks, and the rules below are the contract they check. Where the rules leave something open, decide, keep it consistent everywhere, and write it down.

# 1. Files and boundaries

- `package.json` exists (type module); add a "test" script so `npm test` runs every test with node:test. No dependencies of any kind, no build step.
- `src/` holds the core (pure JavaScript, no DOM, no timers, no randomness other than the seeded generator below) and the renderer. The core must run in Node; the renderer only in the browser.
- `index.html` at the root loads three.js from exactly this URL with a plain script tag: `https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/three.js/0.160.0/three.min.js` (the global `THREE`). Nothing else is loaded from the network. The page loads `src/main.js` as a module script with a relative path and must work from a file:// URL in Chrome started with `--allow-file-access-from-files` (the screenshot tool and the checks do that) or from any static file server; no build step, no bundler.
- Never use eval, new Function, node:vm, child_process, or dynamic code loading. The core modules (rng, map, fov, path, game) must not read the clock or Math.random; the page may use Math.random only to pick the seed of a new game.
- A custom tool named `screenshot` is available in this project: it opens an HTML file in headless Chrome, returns a screenshot and the page's console messages and errors. Use it whenever you change the page or the renderer; a page with console errors is not done.

# 2. Random numbers (`src/rng.js`)

`createRng(seed)` returns a generator implementing mulberry32 over the 32-bit unsigned seed `seed >>> 0`:

```
next(): state = (state + 0x6D2B79F5) >>> 0; t = state; t = Math.imul(t ^ (t >>> 15), t | 1); t ^= t + Math.imul(t ^ (t >>> 7), t | 61); return ((t ^ (t >>> 14)) >>> 0) / 4294967296;
```

`next()` returns a float in [0, 1); `int(max)` returns `Math.floor(next() * max)` (an integer in [0, max)); `pick(array)` returns `array[int(array.length)]`; `state` is readable and writable (the 32-bit unsigned number, always kept in that range), so a game can serialize it and restore it. For seed 123 the first three `next()` values are 0.7872516233474016, 0.1785435655619949, 0.49531551403924823.

# 3. Levels (`src/map.js`)

`generateLevel(seed, depth)` returns `{ width, height, tiles, rooms, start, stairs }`:

- `width` is 60 and `height` is 30. `tiles` is an array of `height` strings of `width` characters: `#` wall, `.` floor, `>` stairs down. Every tile on the outer border is a wall.
- Between 6 and 12 rooms: `rooms` is an array of `{ x, y, w, h }` describing rectangles of floor tiles (w and h between 3 and 10). Rooms never touch: for any two rooms there is at least one wall tile between them in every direction (the rectangles enlarged by one tile do not overlap). Rooms are connected by corridors of floor tiles.
- Every floor tile (and the stairs) is reachable from `start` by 8-directional movement over non-wall tiles.
- `start` is a floor tile inside the first room; `stairs` is a tile inside another room: the room whose centre `(x + w / 2, y + h / 2)` is farthest from `start` (Euclidean distance; the first such room in `rooms` on a tie). For depth below 5 the stairs tile is `>`; on depth 5 (the last one) there is no `>` anywhere and `stairs` is a plain floor tile where the Amulet lies.
- The same seed and depth always produce the identical level; generation uses only `createRng(seed)`.

Passable tiles are `.` and `>`. Everything else in this document that says "adjacent" or "step" means the 8 neighbouring tiles (Chebyshev distance 1), diagonals included, with no corner-cutting rule.

# 4. Field of view (`src/fov.js`)

`computeFov(tiles, x, y, radius)` returns a Set of strings `"x,y"` of the visible tiles, defined exactly like this: a tile T is visible from the origin O when its Euclidean distance satisfies dx*dx + dy*dy <= radius*radius and every tile on the Bresenham line from O to T, excluding T itself, is not a wall. The origin is always visible. Walls are visible when the line reaches them. The Bresenham line is the integer algorithm:

```
dx = |x1 - x0|; dy = -|y1 - y0|; sx = x0 < x1 ? 1 : -1; sy = y0 < y1 ? 1 : -1; err = dx + dy;
loop: visit (x0, y0); if (x0 == x1 && y0 == y1) stop; e2 = 2 * err; if (e2 >= dy) { err += dy; x0 += sx; } if (e2 <= dx) { err += dx; y0 += sy; }
```

# 5. Pathfinding (`src/path.js`)

`findPath(tiles, from, to, blocked = [])` returns the shortest path from `from` to `to` as an array of `{ x, y }` steps, excluding the start and including the target, moving 8-directionally over passable tiles; `blocked` is a list of `{ x, y }` tiles that count as impassable (except the target itself). It returns `null` when there is no path. Any shortest path is acceptable; its length must be minimal.

# 6. The game (`src/game.js`)

`createGame(options)` creates a game. `options.seed` (integer, default 1) seeds everything. Without a fixture the game generates depth 1 with `generateLevel(levelSeed(seed, 1), 1)` where `levelSeed(seed, depth) = (seed + depth * 7919) >>> 0`, places the player at `start`, and populates the level (section 8). With a fixture the level is exactly what the caller says: `options.map` is an array of row strings (any size, same characters), `options.player` is `{ x, y }`, `options.monsters` is an array of `{ type, x, y }`, `options.items` an array of `{ kind, x, y, amount? }`; a fixture level gets no generated monsters or items and no stairs unless the map contains `>`.

`game.state` is a plain, JSON-serialisable object with at least these fields (extra fields are allowed):

```
{ seed, depth, turn, status,             // status: "playing" | "dead" | "won"
  width, height, tiles,                   // tiles: array of row strings
  visible, explored,                      // visible: array of "x,y" strings; explored: array of row strings of "0"/"1"
  player: { x, y, hp, maxHp, attack, defense, level, xp, gold, inventory, equipment: { weapon, armor } },
  monsters: [ { id, type, x, y, hp, maxHp, attack, defense, xp } ],
  items: [ { id, kind, x, y, amount } ],  // amount only for gold
  log }                                   // array of strings, the most recent last, at most 50 kept
```

The player starts with hp 30, maxHp 30, attack 5, defense 1, level 1, xp 0, gold 0, an empty inventory and no equipment. `visible` is recomputed after every action with `computeFov` from the player's tile with radius 8; `explored` marks every tile that has ever been visible.

`game.act(action)` performs one player action; when the action costs a turn, `turn` increases by one and then every monster takes its turn (section 7). It returns the array of log messages the action produced. Actions:

- `{ type: "move", dx, dy }` with dx, dy in -1..1, not both 0. Into a passable tile with no monster: the player moves (costs a turn). Into a monster: the player attacks it (costs a turn). Into a wall or off the map: nothing happens, no turn, a message such as "There is a wall in the way."
- `{ type: "wait" }`: costs a turn.
- `{ type: "pickup" }`: picks up the items on the player's tile. Gold is never stored: it adds `amount` to `player.gold` (message "You pick up N gold."). The Amulet ends the game: status becomes "won", message "You found the Amulet of Yendor! You win." Every other item goes to the inventory as `{ kind, name }`, which holds at most 10 items; an item that does not fit stays on the floor with the message "Your pack is full." The action costs a turn when at least one item was picked up. With nothing on the tile: no turn, message "There is nothing here."
- `{ type: "use", index }`: uses inventory item `index` (0-based). A potion heals 10 hp, capped at maxHp, and is consumed. A weapon or armor is equipped into the matching slot; the item previously in that slot, if any, returns to the inventory. Costs a turn. An invalid index: no turn, a message.
- `{ type: "drop", index }`: moves the inventory item to the floor at the player's tile (costs a turn). Invalid index: no turn.
- `{ type: "descend" }`: only on a `>` tile; otherwise no turn and a message. On the stairs: depth increases by one, the new level is `generateLevel(levelSeed(seed, depth), depth)` populated per section 8, the player stands on its `start`, visible and explored start over, turn continues counting; the message is "You descend to depth N." It costs a turn, so the new level's monsters act once (none of them starts next to the player).

When status is not "playing", `act` changes nothing and returns [].

Combat is deterministic. The player's effective attack is `attack` plus the equipped weapon's bonus (dagger 1, sword 3); effective defense is `defense` plus the equipped armor's bonus (leather 1, chain 2). Damage dealt = max(1, attacker's effective attack - defender's effective defense). A monster whose hp reaches 0 or less is removed, the player gains its xp, message "You kill the <type>." (before that, "You hit the <type> for N."). A monster attacking the player: message "The <type> hits you for N."; when the player's hp reaches 0 or less, hp is 0, status becomes "dead", message "You die."

Levels: after gaining xp, while `xp >= threshold(level + 1)` with `threshold(L) = 5 * L * (L - 1)` (level 2 at 10 xp, level 3 at 30, level 4 at 60, level 5 at 100): level increases by one, maxHp increases by 5, hp increases by 5 (capped at the new maxHp), attack increases by 1, message "Welcome to level N."

`game.serialize()` returns a JSON string; `loadGame(json)` returns a game whose state and future behaviour are identical to the original (include the rng state). `game.hash()` returns a string: FNV-1a 32-bit hash, as 8 lowercase hex digits, of `JSON.stringify` of the state with every object's keys sorted recursively.

`applyKey(game, key)` maps one key to an action and performs it, returning the messages, or `null` for a key that is not an action: h j k l y u b n move (h left, l right, k up, j down, y up-left, u up-right, b down-left, n down-right; up means y - 1), `.` wait, `g` pickup, `>` descend, digits `1`..`9` use inventory item 0..8. `runScript(game, text)` applies the characters of `text` in order, skipping whitespace and unknown characters.

# 7. Monsters

| type | hp | attack | defense | xp | sight |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| rat | 4 | 2 | 0 | 3 | 5 |
| goblin | 8 | 3 | 1 | 6 | 6 |
| skeleton | 12 | 4 | 2 | 10 | 6 |
| orc | 18 | 6 | 2 | 15 | 7 |
| troll | 30 | 8 | 3 | 30 | 7 |

After each turn-costing player action, monsters act in increasing `id` order, one step or attack each. A monster adjacent to the player attacks. Otherwise, when the player's tile is in `computeFov` from the monster's tile with the monster's sight radius, it takes one step along `findPath` toward the player, treating other monsters as blocked; when no path exists it stays. Otherwise it wanders: with probability one half it stays, else it moves to a random adjacent passable tile that holds no monster and not the player, chosen with the game's rng. Monsters never share a tile with each other or with the player and never enter walls.

# 8. Populating a generated level

On a generated level of depth d: 3 + 2d monsters, each of a type chosen with the rng from the types allowed at that depth (depth 1: rat, goblin; depth 2: rat, goblin, skeleton; depth 3: goblin, skeleton, orc; depth 4: skeleton, orc; depth 5: orc, troll), placed on distinct floor tiles outside the first room. 3 + d items on distinct floor tiles that hold no monster and are not the player's tile: each item is a potion with probability 0.4, gold with 0.3 (amount = 5 + int(16) coins), else one of dagger, sword, leather, chain with equal probability. On depth 5 an additional item of kind "amulet" lies on the level's `stairs` tile. Item ids and monster ids are unique within the game.

# 9. The page and the renderer

`index.html` plus `src/main.js` (a module) and whatever renderer modules you like:

- URL parameters: `seed` (integer) fixes the seed; `script` is a key string applied with `runScript` before the first frame. When either parameter is present the title screen is skipped and the game starts at once; otherwise a title screen with the game's name and controls waits for any key and the seed is random.
- A HUD element with id `hud` whose text contains `HP 30/30`, `Depth 1` and `Turn 0` at the start of a new game (and the current values afterwards), the player's level, xp and gold. A message log element with id `log` showing the last messages. An inventory panel toggled with `i`, listing items by number.
- Keyboard: the keys of section 6, plus arrow keys for the four directions, `R` to restart after death or victory, `?` for help. Death and victory screens.
- The renderer is three.js: floor tiles, walls with height, the stairs, the player and each monster type as distinct low-poly meshes or coloured shapes with a glyph label, items as small shapes; unexplored tiles are not drawn, explored tiles outside the current view are dimmed, visible tiles are lit; a light follows the player; the camera looks down at the player from above and behind and follows smoothly; a hit flashes the target and shakes the screen briefly, a kill spawns a short particle burst; monsters and the player move with a short tween rather than teleporting. A dark palette with a few strong accent colours. Optional: WebAudio beeps for hits and pickups.
- Expose the game as `window.game` for debugging.

# 10. Tests and documentation

Every core module has node:test tests in `test/`; cover generation constraints, field of view, paths, combat numbers, items, levels, stairs, serialization and determinism (the same seed and script give the same hash). Write a README.md: how to play, the controls, the architecture (modules, the state shape, how the renderer reads the state), and how to run the tests. npm test must pass.

tasks.title: Test harness, seeded RNG and boundary guard
tasks.spec:
Set up the project harness and the random number generator (design sections 1, 2, 3).

1) `package.json`: keep `"type": "module"`, keep name/version, add `"scripts": { "test": "node --test test/" }`. Do NOT add `dependencies` or `devDependencies` (an empty or absent field is fine, the boundary test rejects any entry). No build step.

2) `src/rng.js`: export `createRng(seed)` returning `{ get state, set state, next(), int(max), pick(array) }`, implementing mulberry32 exactly as specified in the brief over `seed >>> 0`. `state` is always a 32-bit unsigned number (the setter coerces with `>>> 0`); `next()` advances the state, then computes and returns the value in [0,1); `int(max) = Math.floor(next()*max)`; `pick(a) = a[int(a.length)]`. No other exports, no default export, must not use Math.random or the clock.

3) `test/rng.test.js` (node:test + node:assert/strict): seed 123 gives exactly 0.7872516233474016, 0.1785435655619949, 0.49531551403924823 from three `next()` calls; values stay in [0,1) over many draws; `int(6)` stays in 0..5 and is deterministic; `pick` returns a member and is deterministic; `state` is a uint32 that can be read, copied, written back to a fresh generator and produces the identical continuation; two generators with the same seed produce the same sequence.

4) `test/boundaries.test.js`: with `node:fs`/`node:path`, recursively collect `src/**/*.js` (skip files that do not exist yet; the test must pass on a tree containing only rng.js). Assert: every collected file is free of `eval(`, `new Function`, `node:vm`, `child_process` and dynamic `import(`; `src/rng.js`, `src/map.js`, `src/fov.js`, `src/path.js`, `src/game.js` (those that exist) are free of `Math.random`, `Date.now`, `Date(`, `performance.now`, `setTimeout`, `setInterval`, `process.hrtime`, `require(`; `package.json` has no dependency entries and has a `test` script.

Keep the module and tests small; this task only exists to make `npm test` the project's acceptance command and to freeze the RNG contract every other module depends on.

acceptance.review: Confirm package.json has no dependencies and that the boundary test actually collects src/**.js recursively (add a temporary file to see it fail, then remove it) rather than scanning nothing.

report.summary: Set up the project harness and froze the RNG contract. package.json keeps name/version/type:module and gains a "test" script, with no dependency fields and no build step. src/rng.js exports only createRng(seed) -> { get state, set state, next(), int(max), pick(array) } implementing mulberry32 exactly as specified over seed >>> 0, with the state always a uint32 (setter coerces with >>> 0) so games can serialize and restore it; no clock and no Math.random. test/rng.test.js covers the documented seed-123 values, range over 20000 draws, int/pick determinism and ranges, state read/copy/write-back continuation, setter and seed coercion, same-seed sequence identity, and the exact exported surface. test/boundaries.test.js recursively collects src/**/*.js and enforces the forbidden-API rules plus core-module purity, and checks package.json for dependency entries, a test script, type: module, and absence of node_modules. Only src/rng.js, test/rng.test.js and test/boundaries.test.js exist in src/ and test/, so every "if it exists" guard in the boundary test is currently exercised gracefully.
report.evidence: `npm test` -> exit 0, 14 tests, 14 pass, 0 fail. `node --test test/rng.test.js` -> exit 0, 9 pass. Seed 123 gives 0.7872516233474016, 0.1785435655619949, 0.49531551403924823 (verified against the brief). Recursion review: planted src/__probe_dir__/deep/__probe.js containing `eval("1 + 1")`; `node --test test/boundaries.test.js` then failed with "src/__probe_dir__/deep/__probe.js: eval is never allowed (found \"eval(\")", proving files two levels deep are collected; after `rm -rf` the suite passed again and `find src -type f` shows only src/rng.js. `git status --short` shows M package.json and untracked src/ and test/; no commits, nothing outside scope touched.
decisions: The test script is `node --test "test/**/*.test.js"` rather than the design's literal `node --test test/`, because this environment is Node v26.0.0 where a directory argument to --test is no longer expanded and instead fails with MODULE_NOT_FOUND (reproduced on a scratch directory, so it is Node behaviour). The glob form works on Node 22+ and here, and also covers nested test directories. Tests stay flat in test/*.test.js per the design layout.
src/rng.js uses a module-level STEP constant for 0x6D2B79F5 to keep next() readable; the arithmetic is otherwise character-for-character the brief's algorithm.

The boundary test skips core modules and src files that do not exist yet, so it passes on a tree containing only rng.js as the task requires, while still asserting that the scan collected at least src/rng.js (so an empty scan cannot silently pass).

Room for other tasks: the boundary test reads src recursive, so map.js, fov.js, path.js, game.js and any src/renderer/*.js added later are picked up automatically; renderer files are only subject to the project-wide forbidden-API rules, not the core purity rules.

tasks.title: Field of view (src/fov.js)
tasks.spec:
Implement `src/fov.js` per design section 3 and brief section 4.

`export function computeFov(tiles, x, y, radius)` returns a `Set` of `"x,y"` strings. A tile T is visible from origin O when `dx*dx + dy*dy <= radius*radius` and every tile on the Bresenham line from O to T, excluding T itself, is not a wall (`#`). The origin is always visible. Walls are visible when the line reaches them. Use the exact integer Bresenham loop from the brief. Coordinates outside `tiles` are skipped (never added); `radius` 0 yields only the origin. `tiles` is an array of equal-length row strings of any size.

This module must not import from `src/map.js` or any other project module: keep a private one-line passability/wall check so the task stays independent of the map task, which runs in parallel.

`test/fov.test.js`: hand-built small ASCII maps with expected visible sets, covering: open room (a full radius block minus the tiles outside the distance), origin always visible and visible through anything, an isolated wall tile adjacent to the origin, a wall blocking the tiles directly behind it while the wall itself is visible, a longer wall casting a shadow, diagonal sight lines through a doorway, the exact radius boundary (a tile exactly at distance `radius` visible, one beyond it not), radius 0, and a narrow corridor. Include at least one assertion computed against an independent brute-force reimplementation of the rule written inside the test file (line-walk + distance) for a couple of random-ish fixtures, so the implementation is checked against the definition rather than against itself.

acceptance.review: Check the Bresenham loop matches the brief character for character, and that the test's brute-force oracle is an independent implementation, not a copy of the module.

report.summary:
Implemented `src/fov.js` — `computeFov(tiles, x, y, radius)` returns a `Set` of `"x,y"` strings by testing every in-grid tile in the radius bounding box for `dx*dx + dy*dy <= radius*radius` and then walking the brief's exact integer Bresenham line from the origin to that tile, rejecting it if any visited tile other than the target is a wall. The module has no imports (private one-line wall check, no dependency on src/map.js) and no DOM/clock/randomness, so it stays independent of the parallel map task.

`test/fov.test.js` has 14 tests: hand-built ASCII fixtures with hardcoded expected sets for an open room (radius block), the exact distance boundary (radius-5 Pythagorean offsets), the origin (always visible, including a wall origin and radius 0), an isolated adjacent wall, a wall hiding the tiles directly behind it, a longer wall casting a shadow, diagonal sight through a doorway, a straight corridor, a corridor corner, tiles outside the grid, non-mutation, and two definition-based comparisons against an independent brute-force oracle.

Key finding for later tasks: the rule is aggressive — around a corridor corner only the first tile past the bend is visible, and a single wall tile hides the three tiles diagonally/straight behind it. That is what the brief's definition produces, and the fixtures pin it down.
report.evidence:
Acceptance commands run from the project root, both exit 0:
- `node --test test/fov.test.js` → 14/14 pass, 0 fail.
- `npm test` → 45 tests, 45 pass, 0 fail (includes the boundary guard, which passes with src/fov.js present, and the concurrently added map/path/game tests are unaffected).

Oracle validation before writing the tests: I compared my test's independent line formulation (closed-form: step once per tile along the dominant axis, minor coordinate = floor((2*i*minor + major) / (2*major))) against the brief's error-term loop for all 390,625 lines with coordinates in -12..12 — 0 mismatches, and the brief's loop always terminated. Fixture expected sets were derived from that oracle and then hand-verified tile by tile (e.g. the wall tile is visible while 2,1/3,1 behind it are not; the diagonal (1,1)->(2,2)->(3,3) through a doorway is visible while (1,3) is not). The module then matched every hardcoded set on the first run, and matched the oracle over all 9 fixtures x every origin x radii {0,1,2,3,6,40} plus 40 generated maps (deterministic LCG, with '#'/'>'/'.').

Edge behaviour checked directly: radius 2.5 → 21 tiles, radius Infinity → whole grid, radius NaN → empty, empty map → empty, ragged rows handled, '>' does not block sight, repeated calls identical.
decisions: A wall tile at the origin is visible (the origin is on its own line and only the target is exempt from the line check) but blocks every other tile. The brief's two statements coexist under this literal reading; in the game the player never stands on a wall, so this only shows up in tests.

A negative radius returns an empty Set (no tile, not even the origin, can satisfy distance <= a negative radius); radius 0 returns exactly the origin. NaN radius also yields an empty Set (all comparisons are false).

Tiles outside the grid are never added to the result and never block a line: a walk between two in-grid tiles stays inside their bounding box, so the only case where this matters is an origin outside the map, which then simply reports no in-grid tile with itself absent.
Bounding-box iteration uses Math.ceil/Math.floor of the radius, so a non-integer radius scans the right tiles (the exact test remains dx*dx + dy*dy <= radius*radius).

The test's oracle is a closed-form rounding formulation of the same line rule rather than the brief's error-term loop, verified equivalent over 390,625 lines; the tests never call into src/fov.js to build an expectation.
openIssues: None. Note for the game/renderer tasks only: the brief's FOV rule is deliberately strict, so visibility around corners and behind single wall tiles is limited (a one-tile-wide corridor shows roughly two tiles past a bend). Fixtures in test/fov.test.js record the exact expected sets if a renderer check needs them.

report.summary: No change was required in my scope: the reported failure was a transient cross-task failure in another executor's files. `test/map.test.js:235` asserted `generateLevel(seed, depth)` deep-equals `generateLevelRng(createRng(levelSeed(seed, depth)), depth)` — a determinism test entirely inside the map task (src/map.js imports only src/rng.js, and no module in the tree imports src/fov.js except the boundary test's CORE filename list). The map executor was still mid-edit (map.test.js changed at 03:20:35, after my report), and their fix has since landed. Re-running now gives a green suite, so src/fov.js and test/fov.test.js are unchanged from the version I reported (mtimes 03:18:39 and 03:19:07, both untouched).
report.evidence:
Ran both acceptance commands from the project root just now:
- `node --test test/fov.test.js` → exit 0, 14 tests, 14 pass, 0 fail.
- `npm test` → exit 0, 55 tests, 55 pass, 0 fail (was 45 tests with 1 failure at the time of the failed acceptance; the map task's suite grew and its failing assertion now holds).

Scope check: `grep -rn "fov" src/ test/` returns only test/fov.test.js, src/fov.js and the CORE list in test/boundaries.test.js; `src/map.js` imports only './rng.js', so the failure could not have been caused by fov.js. File mtimes confirm src/fov.js and test/fov.test.js are byte-identical to what I submitted.
decisions: Not fixing or touching files outside my scope (src/map.js, test/map.test.js): the failing assertion belonged to the map task, which was actively editing those files at that moment, and editing them from here would collide with that executor.
openIssues: Cross-task flakiness: `npm test` runs every executor's tests, so a parallel task's in-progress failure fails this task's acceptance too. Here it resolved itself; if it recurs, the map task's determinism test is the place to look, not fov.js.

tasks.title: 8-directional shortest paths (src/path.js)
tasks.spec:
Implement `src/path.js` per design section 3 and brief section 5.

`export function findPath(tiles, from, to, blocked = [])` returns the shortest path as an array of `{x, y}` steps, excluding the start and including the target, moving 8-directionally over passable tiles (`.` or `>`), where `blocked` (a list of `{x, y}`) counts as impassable except the target itself. Returns `null` when no path exists. `from` equal to `to` returns `[]`. A wall or out-of-grid target returns `null`. Use a BFS with the fixed neighbour order from the design (dy -1..1 outer, dx -1..1 inner, skipping 0,0) so results are deterministic run to run. Do not implement diagonal corner restrictions.

No imports from other project modules (private wall/passable check), so this task stays independent of the map task.

`test/path.test.js`: straight corridor and its exact length; a diagonal-only walk; an open field where the returned length equals the Chebyshev distance (the optimum for 8-directional uniform cost) for many from/to pairs; unreachable case returns null; `from === to` returns `[]`; `blocked` tiles are avoided and a wall of blocked tiles that fully encloses the target returns null; a blocked tile that equals the target is still reachable (the exception); every step of every returned path is adjacent to the previous one and passable; the target appears exactly once as the last step; determinism across repeated calls.

acceptance.review: Confirm length minimality is asserted (Chebyshev distance in open space, not merely 'some path'), and that blocked handling really exempts the target.

report.summary:
Implemented `src/path.js` (BFS shortest 8-directional paths) and `test/path.test.js`; both acceptance commands pass.

`findPath(tiles, from, to, blocked = [])` explores with the design's fixed neighbour order (dy -1..1 outer, dx -1..1 inner, skipping 0,0) and returns as soon as the target is first discovered, so results are deterministic and minimal (BFS over uniform-cost steps). The start is excluded and the target included in the returned array. `from === to` (compared by value, not identity) returns `[]`; a wall or out-of-grid target returns `null`; an unreachable target returns `null`. Blocked tiles go into a `"x,y"` key Set with the target key removed, which implements the "except the target itself" exception exactly. No corner-cutting rule: a diagonal step is legal whenever the destination is passable. The module imports nothing and keeps a private one-line `isPassable` (`'.'` or `'>'`), so it stays independent of `src/map.js`.

The test file covers the requested cases: exact walks in straight and vertical corridors, a lone diagonal step where both orthogonal cells are walls (and its reverse), a pure diagonal walk, Chebyshev-length equality in an open field for ~1500 from/to pairs, stairs (`>`) passability, unreachable → null, `from === to` → `[]` (including on a wall tile), wall/out-of-grid target → null, blocked tiles avoided (including a slab that forces a 7-step detour where the straight walk is 6), a blocked tile cutting the only route → null, an 8-neighbour blocked ring around the target → null, a blocked tile equal to the target still reachable (plus neighbours-of-target blocking still returning null, proving only the target is exempt), per-step adjacency/passability/target-uniqueness invariants, and determinism over 20 repeated calls with an unmutated blocked list. Additionally, minimality is validated against an independent Bellman-Ford relaxation oracle over all floor pairs of a fixed obstacle maze, with and without blocked lists.

Out of scope for me but worth noting: `npm test` currently runs only the rng, boundary and path suites, because the other executors' modules and test files are not in the tree yet.

tasks.title: Level generation (src/map.js)
tasks.spec:
Implement `src/map.js` per design sections 3 and 5 (algorithm frozen there so monster placement and determinism stay reproducible across sessions).

Exports: `WIDTH = 60`, `HEIGHT = 30`, `isPassable(ch)` (`.` or `>`), `levelSeed(seed, depth) => (seed + depth * 7919) >>> 0`, `generateLevelRng(rng, depth)` (takes an existing generator and draws from it), and `generateLevel(seed, depth)` = `generateLevelRng(createRng(seed >>> 0), depth)`. Return `{ width, height, tiles, rooms, start, stairs }` with `tiles` an array of 30 row strings of 60 characters using `#`, `.`, `>`; every border tile a wall; 6..12 rooms of `w`,`h` in 3..10 with pairwise-disjoint 1-tile-enlarged rectangles and chained L-corridors connecting consecutive room centres; `start` the floored centre of `rooms[0]`; `stairs` the floored centre of the non-first room whose centre is farthest (Euclidean, first in `rooms` order on a tie) from `start`; `>` at `stairs` when `depth < 5` and no `>` anywhere plus a plain `.` at `stairs` when `depth >= 5`. Every floor tile and the stairs must be reachable from `start` by 8-directional movement. Deterministic for a given seed and depth.

The frozen loop in design section 5 (draw order, retry/fallback rule, corridor axis choice) matters: the population task continues drawing monster/item positions from the same generator instance afterwards.

`test/map.test.js`: for depths 1..5 and seeds 1..25 assert dimensions, row lengths, allowed characters only, all-border walls, room count 6..12, room sizes and in-bounds placement, pairwise enlarged-rectangle disjointness, `start` inside `rooms[0]` and passable, `stairs` inside a non-first room and equal to an independently recomputed farthest-centre choice, `isPassable(tiles[stairs.y][stairs.x])`, exactly one `>` at `stairs` for depths 1..4 and none anywhere for depth 5, and full reachability: a flood fill from `start` over passable tiles reaches every `.` and `>` tile. Also assert `generateLevel(seed, depth)` deep-equals itself on repeat and that `generateLevelRng` continues a generator (two calls on the same instance give different levels).

acceptance.review: Confirm the corridor/room ordering in the code matches design section 5 exactly (the population task depends on the generator continuing after generation), and that the reachability assertion really floods the whole grid.

report.summary:
Implemented src/map.js (level generation) per design sections 3 and 5, plus test/map.test.js.

src/map.js exports exactly the frozen surface: WIDTH (60), HEIGHT (30), isPassable(ch) ('.' or '>'), levelSeed(seed, depth) = (seed + depth * 7919) >>> 0, generateLevelRng(rng, depth) and generateLevel(seed, depth) = generateLevelRng(createRng(seed >>> 0), depth). It imports only ./rng.js and is pure (no clock, DOM, timers or ambient randomness). Returned level is { width, height, tiles, rooms, start, stairs } with 30 row strings of 60 characters of '#', '.' and '>'.

Algorithm is the frozen one, because the population task keeps drawing from the same generator afterwards: 1 rng.int(7) for the room target (6..12), then 4 rng.int draws per placement attempt (w, h, x, y — drawn even when rejected, x = 1 + int(WIDTH - w - 2), y = 1 + int(HEIGHT - h - 2)) until the target count is reached or 4000 attempts are spent; a round with fewer than 6 rooms is discarded and redrawn with the generator continuing, up to 20 rounds, then a fixed 6-room fallback layout. Rooms are carved after placement, then exactly one rng.next() per consecutive room pair picks the corridor axis (< 0.5 = horizontal first), carving '.' over '#' only. start = floored centre of rooms[0]; stairs = floored centre of the non-first room with the farthest centre (squared Euclidean from start, first on a tie); '>' at stairs for depth < 5, plain '.' and no '>' anywhere for depth >= 5.

test/map.test.js covers depths 1..5 x seeds 1..25: dimensions and row lengths, allowed characters, all-border walls, 6..12 rooms with w,h in 3..10 inside the border with pairwise disjoint 1-tile-enlarged rectangles, start as the floored centre of rooms[0] and passable, stairs against an independently recomputed farthest-centre choice and inside a non-first room, isPassable at the stairs, exactly one '>' at stairs for depths 1..4 and none anywhere for depth 5, and full reachability via a local 8-directional flood fill from start that visits every passable tile of the grid. It also asserts deep equality of generateLevel on repeat, that generateLevelRng advances and continues a generator instance, and drives the 20-round give-up/fallback path with a stub generator to confirm the invariants survive it.
report.evidence:
Commands run from the project root, all exit 0:
- `node --test test/map.test.js` -> 11 tests, pass 11, fail 0, exit 0 (spec reporter output lists all 11 test names as passing).
- `npm test` -> 56 tests, pass 56, fail 0, exit 0 (map, rng, path and boundaries suites all green).
Extra checks outside the suite:
- Stress run over 4000 map seeds x depths 1..5 = 20000 levels: 0 failures for room count 6..12, room separation, border walls, reachability (flood size equals the passable tile count), stairs character and '>' count; observed rooms min/max 6/12, minimum floor tiles 177.
- Instrumented copy of the placement loop over 2000 map seeds x depths 1..5 (10000 rounds): 0 rounds needed a redo and the 4000-draw cap was never reached (max 1943 draws in a round, average 35.5), so the retry/fallback branch is effectively dead code in practice.
- `node -e "import('./src/map.js')..."` prints exports: HEIGHT, WIDTH, generateLevel, generateLevelRng, isPassable, levelSeed.
Review points: the corridor/room ordering in src/map.js matches design section 5 exactly (placement draws, then carving, then one rng.next() per consecutive room pair in rooms order), so a caller can continue drawing monster/item positions from the same generator instance; the reachability assertion really floods the whole grid from start and asserts every single passable tile is in the flooded set rather than sampling.
decisions: generateLevel(seed, depth) treats its first argument as the map seed directly (createRng(seed >>> 0)); it does not apply levelSeed itself, matching the design's one-line wrapper and the game calling generateLevel(levelSeed(seed, depth), depth). Consequence: generateLevel(3, 1) and generateLevel(3, 2) share a layout and differ only in the stairs tile.

Frozen rng consumption for downstream population: after generateLevelRng returns, the stream has consumed 1 int for the room target, 4 ints per placement attempt and 1 next() per consecutive room pair; map.js draws nothing afterwards, so game.js can keep drawing from the same instance.

Concrete fallback layout for the pathological fewer-than-6-rooms case: 6 rooms of 10x6 at x in {3, 24, 45}, y in {3, 16}, which keeps one wall tile between enlarged rectangles on every edge. Measured as unreachable in practice (no redo round in 10000 rounds), but implemented and covered by a test using a stub generator whose int() is always 0 and next() always 0.9.

test/map.test.js uses its own local passable() and flood fill rather than importing isPassable from src/map.js, so the reachability check is not circular; the farthest-centre stairs choice is likewise recomputed independently from the reported start and rooms.

tasks.title: Game state, level setup, actions, monster AI, combat, serialization
tasks.spec:
Create `src/game.js` with the pieces of the core that do not involve the player's items (items are populated in state but only picked up/used/dropped by the next task).

Implement, per design sections 4, 5, 6, 7 and 12:
1. `createGame(options)`: `options.seed` integer default 1. Without `options.map`, generate depth 1 with `generateLevelRng(createRng(levelSeed(seed, 1)), 1)`, place the player on `start`, populate per design section 7 (3+2d monsters from the depth's allowed types on distinct floor tiles outside `rooms[0]`, 3+d items with potion 0.4 / gold 0.3 amount `5 + int(16)` / dagger,sword,leather,chain otherwise, ids from the counters). With `options.map` (row strings, any size) use it verbatim, place `options.player` (default `{x:1,y:1}` if absent), `options.monsters` (`{type,x,y}` with table stats), `options.items` (`{kind,x,y,amount}`), all with fresh ids; no generated monsters/items/stairs unless the map contains `>`.
2. Full `state` shape including the extra fields `rng`, `nextMonsterId`, `nextItemId` (design section 4). `visible` sorted by y then x; `explored` row strings of `0`/`1`; `log` capped at 50.
3. `game.act(action)` with the frozen pipeline: move (wall message `"There is a wall in the way."`, target monster → player attack, else move), wait, descend (`"There are no stairs here."` off stairs; on stairs depth += 1, new generated+populated level, player on `start`, visible/explored reset, message `"You descend to depth N."`, costs a turn so the new monsters act once), monster turn loop in increasing id order (adjacent → attack; else player visible via `computeFov` with the monster's sight → one `findPath` step with other monsters blocked; else wander with the fixed rng order; stop the loop when status changes), damage `max(1, effectiveAttack - effectiveDefense)` with equipment bonuses dagger 1 / sword 3 / leather 1 / chain 2 read from `player.equipment`, kill/xp/level-up rules and messages, death rules, and `visible`/`explored` recomputed after every action. Return only the player action's messages.
4. `serialize()`, `loadGame(json)`, `hash()` (FNV-1a 32-bit, 8 lowercase hex digits, of the key-sorted recursive JSON), both refreshing `state.rng` first. `export { levelSeed }` re-exported from `src/map.js`, plus `export const MONSTERS` and `export const ITEM_KINDS`.
5. `applyKey`/`runScript` are NOT part of this task (the next task adds them); unknown action types return `[]` with no turn, so `pickup`/`use`/`drop` are silently ignored for now.

`test/game.test.js`: fixture-driven tests for the state shape and defaults (hp 30/30, attack 5, defense 1, level 1, turn 0, status playing), FOV/explored updates after a move, wall bump (no turn, message), wait and turn counting, monster adjacency attack damage (`max(1, atk-def)`), monster kill/xp/level-up thresholds (10/30/60/100 xp), player death (`hp` clamped to 0, status dead), generated-level population counts and depth-allowed types, descend message/depth/turn continuation/visible reset, `serialize`/`loadGame` round-trip (state deep-equal and `loadGame(g.serialize()).serialize() === g.serialize()`), `hash()` format `^[0-9a-f]{8}$`, and monster AI behaviours (a visible monster steps closer, a blocked one stays, monsters never overlap the player or each other, wander uses the rng deterministically).

acceptance.review: Verify the act() pipeline order (turn increment, monster loop, FOV refresh, log cap, returned messages = player messages only) and the exact rng consumption order in the monster turn against design sections 6 and 7.

report.summary:
Created `src/game.js` (546 lines) with the deterministic core pieces that do not involve the player's items, and `test/game.test.js` (730 lines, 21 node:test cases).

src/game.js exports `createGame(options)`, `loadGame(json)`, `levelSeed` (re-exported from src/map.js), `MONSTERS` and `ITEM_KINDS`. A game object is `{ state, act, serialize, hash }` with plain JSON state in the frozen design shape plus the extra `rng`, `nextMonsterId`, `nextItemId` fields.

- createGame: without `options.map` it builds depth 1 from `generateLevelRng(createRng(levelSeed(seed,1)),1)` and then keeps drawing from that same generator to populate (3+2d monsters on distinct floor tiles outside rooms[0], tile-then-type; 3+d items, tile-then-kind with potion <0.4 / gold <0.7 (amount 5+int(16)) / otherwise one of dagger,sword,leather,chain; amulet on level.stairs at depth >= 5). With `options.map` the rows are used verbatim, the player defaults to {x:1,y:1}, listed monsters get table stats and listed items are placed with fresh ids from the counters, and no level content is generated.
- act implements the frozen pipeline: status guard -> player action -> on a turn cost, turn += 1 and then the monster loop in increasing id order (adjacent -> attack; else player tile visible via computeFov with the monster's sight -> one findPath step with other monsters blocked; else wander with the rng order: one next() half-check always consumed, then int() only when a move happens) -> visible/explored refreshed after every action including free ones -> log truncated to 50 -> only the player action's own messages returned. move/wait/descend are implemented; pickup/use/drop fall through as unknown actions (no turn, []), ready for the items task.
- Combat is max(1, effectiveAttack - effectiveDefense) with dagger 1 / sword 3 / leather 1 / chain 2 read from player.equipment via ITEM_KINDS; kill/xp/level-up (threshold 5*L*(L-1)) and death (hp clamped to 0, status "dead") follow the design messages exactly.
- serialize()/loadGame()/hash() (FNV-1a 32-bit over the recursively key-sorted JSON, 8 lowercase hex digits) both refresh state.rng first.

All acceptance commands pass.
report.evidence:
`npm test` from the project root: tests 77, pass 77, fail 0 (21 of those are test/game.test.js; the rest are the rng, boundary, map, fov and path suites written by other tasks).

The game suite covers: frozen tables and the levelSeed re-export; fresh-game state shape/defaults (hp 30/30, attack 5, defense 1, level 1, turn 0, status playing, equipment nulls, 60x30 tiles, explored rows of /[01]{60}/, counters at 6/5); generated depth-1 level matching an independently regenerated level plus monster/item placement rules (outside room 0, allowed types, table stats, no shared tiles, unique ids, gold amount 5..20 and no amount on other kinds); fixture verbatim handling with fresh ids and no added stairs; wall bump (no turn, "There is a wall in the way."); wait/move turn counting and unknown/zero-move actions ignored; items not blocking movement; visible/explored refreshed after every action (compared against a direct computeFov call), sort order y-then-x, explored only growing; attack damage and the exchange log; all four equipment bonuses plus max(1, ...) clamping; level-ups at 10/30/60/100 xp (single and multi-level jump, and one xp short of the threshold); death with hp clamped to 0, status dead, five troll hits then "You die.", and all subsequent actions returning [] without changing the state; descend (message "You descend to depth 2.", turn continuation, 7 monsters, 5 items, visible/explored reset, hp unchanged, off-stairs message with no turn); a full dive to depth 5 checking per-depth monster counts/types/id uniqueness and item counts with the amulet and no '>' anywhere; serialize/loadGame round-trip (state deep-equal, byte-identical serialize, identical behaviour over a shared action script) and a load-load twin check; hash format ^[0-9a-f]{8}$ with same-seed/same-script stability, sensitivity to the state, and the seed 1 default; monster AI stepping along findPath's first step, a monster blocked by another staying put while the free one advances, 40 turns of no-overlap/no-wall invariants, and deterministic wander (same seed identical, different seeds diverge); the 50-message log cap.

Extra scratch checks (node -e, not committed): createGame does not mutate the caller's options object; a 400-turn two-game action script stayed bit-identical (equal hashes) while re-checking no monster overlap, no monster in a wall, no monster on the player, log <= 50 and hp <= maxHp after every turn.
decisions: ITEM_KINDS is a table keyed by kind, each value { name, slot, bonus }: potion {name:'Potion',slot:null,bonus:0}, gold {name:'gold'}, dagger {name:'Dagger',slot:'weapon',bonus:1}, sword {name:'Sword',slot:'weapon',bonus:3}, leather {name:'Leather armor',slot:'armor',bonus:1}, chain {name:'Chain mail',slot:'armor',bonus:2}, amulet {name:'Amulet of Yendor',slot:null,bonus:0}. Combat already reads player.equipment.weapon/armor through this table, so the equipment-bonus tests run before the items task exists.
applyKey/runScript are deliberately absent (the next task adds them). pickup/use/drop are unknown action types here: no turn, no message, [] returned, and the game state is untouched.

descend moves the player onto the new level's `start` BEFORE population, so the item rule "not the player's tile" means the start tile. This is load-bearing: the excluded tile changes the row-major candidate list length, which changes which indices rng.int picks.

descend replaces the live generator with createRng(levelSeed(state.seed, newDepth)); state.rng is refreshed only by serialize()/hash() per the design's explicit decision, so immediately after a descend state.rng still mirrors the previous level's generator until the next serialize() or hash(). act never writes state.rng, and createGame sets it once at construction.
A fixture game's wandering rng is createRng(levelSeed(seed, 1)) — the same derivation as a generated level — so a fixture and a generated game with the same seed wander identically.
options.depth is not supported: a non-fixture game is always depth 1 as the brief states, and deeper levels are reached only through descend. Fixture games are always depth 1.

Monster types are clamped to depth 5's row for depth > 5, and the amulet is placed for any depth >= 5 (a fixture with a '>' at depth 5 can therefore descend to a depth-6 level that still holds an amulet).
move with non-integer or out-of-range dx/dy is ignored exactly like the 0,0 case (no turn, no message).
openIssues: The task text mentions "design sections 4, 5, 6, 7 and 12", but the design document only has sections 1-11; I implemented against 4 (state), 5 (level generation, consumed via map.js), 6 (game rules) and 7 (population, extended to depth >= 5).
Item pickup/use/drop and applyKey/runScript are intentionally not implemented here; until the items/keys task lands, those action types are silent no-ops and an amulet can be placed but not taken.

state.rng is stale after a descend until serialize()/hash() is called (per the design's explicit decision). Anything that round-trips through JSON.stringify(game.state) directly instead of game.serialize() will restore the wrong generator state.

test/game.test.js reaches deeper levels for the population test by writing game.state.player.x/y onto the '>' tile before calling descend, since there is no public teleport and walking there could be a long fight; the state is plain data so this is safe, but it is worth knowing when reading the test.

tasks.title: Items, equipment, inventory, key mapping and determinism tests
tasks.spec:
Extend `src/game.js` with the player-item actions and the input mapping, per design sections 6.1, 6.3, 6.4 and 6.5. Do not change the interfaces other tasks rely on (`createGame`, `act`, `serialize`, `hash`, `state` shape).

1. `pickup`: process items on the player's tile in ascending id; gold adds `amount` to `player.gold` and logs `"You pick up N gold."`; the amulet removes the item, sets `status = "won"` and logs `"You found the Amulet of Yendor! You win."`; other items go to the inventory as `{ kind, name }` (max 10) with `"You pick up the <name>."`, else stay on the floor with `"Your pack is full."`; costs a turn iff something was removed from the floor; nothing on the tile → no turn, `"There is nothing here."`.
2. `use(index)`: invalid index → no turn, `"You have no such item."`; potion heals 10 capped at maxHp, is consumed, costs a turn; dagger/sword equip to `equipment.weapon`, leather/chain to `equipment.armor`, displacing the previous item back to the inventory (dropped on the player's tile if the pack is full), costs a turn. Equipping changes effective attack/defense as already implemented in the game-world task.
3. `drop(index)`: invalid index → no turn; otherwise the item moves to the floor at the player's tile as `{ id: nextItemId++, kind, x, y }` and costs a turn.
4. `applyKey(game, key)` and `runScript(game, text)` exactly as in design section 6.5 (h j k l y u b n, `.`, `g`, `>`, `1`-`9`, `null` for anything else, whitespace/unknown skipped).
5. Names: potion `"Potion"`, dagger `"Dagger"`, sword `"Sword"`, leather `"Leather armor"`, chain `"Chain mail"`, amulet `"Amulet of Yendor"`.

Extend `test/game.test.js` (keep the existing tests passing; adjust them only if this task's behaviour genuinely changes them) with: gold pickup amount and message, item pickup into the inventory with name, the 10-item cap and `"Your pack is full."`, the amulet win, `"There is nothing here."`, potion healing capped at maxHp and consumption, equip/unequip round trip, weapon bonus visibly changing damage (dagger 1, sword 3) and armor bonus reducing incoming damage, drop placing the item on the floor, invalid use/drop index costing no turn, `applyKey` for every mapped key plus `null` for unknown keys, `runScript` skipping whitespace/unknown characters, and the determinism requirement: two games created with the same seed and driven by the same script produce identical `hash()` values, and serializing mid-game, reloading with `loadGame` and continuing the same script yields the same hash as running it straight through.

acceptance.review: Confirm equipment bonuses really flow into combat damage, that no-turn paths never increment `turn`, and that the two determinism assertions compare hashes after the same number of actions.

report.summary:
Extended src/game.js with the player-item actions and the input mapping, and extended test/game.test.js to cover them.

In src/game.js (all inside the existing act() pipeline, so `visible`/`explored` refresh, the 50-entry log truncation and the monster turn are unchanged):
- `pickup`: items on the player's tile are processed in ascending id; gold adds its amount to player.gold ("You pick up N gold."), the amulet sets status "won" ("You found the Amulet of Yendor! You win."), any other item enters the pack as { kind, name } when the pack holds fewer than 10 ("You pick up the <name>.") and otherwise stays on the floor ("Your pack is full."). The action costs a turn iff at least one item actually left the floor; an empty tile gives "There is nothing here." and no turn.
- `use(index)`: a non-integer, negative or out-of-range index gives "You have no such item." and no turn. A potion restores min(maxHp, hp + 10) hp, is consumed, costs a turn and reports the amount actually restored. A dagger/sword goes to equipment.weapon and leather/chain to equipment.armor, both going through the existing ITEM_KINDS bonus table, so the combat formula picks the bonus up; the displaced item returns to the pack (appended last) or, if the pack is full, is dropped on the player's tile. An amulet (or any item with no slot and no effect) cannot be used and still costs a turn.
- `drop(index)`: an invalid index gives "You have no such item." and no turn; otherwise the item leaves the pack and lands on the player's tile as { id: nextItemId++, kind, x, y }.
- New exports `applyKey(game, key)` and `runScript(game, text)` implementing design section 6.5 exactly (h j k l y u b n, ".", "g", ">" and the digits 1-9, `null` for anything else, whitespace and unknown characters skipped by runScript). The key table sits on a null prototype so inherited property names can never be treated as keys.

test/game.test.js gained 13 cases (94 tests total, all passing): gold pickup, multi-item pickup in id order with names, the 10-item cap plus the free "pack is full" case and gold bypassing the cap, the amulet win (and the frozen game afterwards), "There is nothing here.", potion healing capped at maxHp with consumption, equip/swap round trips for weapons and armor plus the crafted full-pack displacement case, equipment bonuses flowing into real damage numbers through the actual pickup/use path (skeleton: 3 bare, 4 dagger, 6 sword; troll: 7 bare, 6 leather, 5 chain), drop to the floor with a fresh id and re-pickup, invalid use/drop indices costing no turn, every mapped key in applyKey, `null` for 40 unmapped keys including "toString"/"__proto__", runScript skipping whitespace and unknowns, and the two determinism assertions (same seed + same script => identical hash; serialize mid-game, loadGame, continue the same script => same hash and same turn count as running straight through).

One pre-existing test was adjusted because its premise genuinely changed: pickup/use/drop are no longer unknown actions, so they were moved out of the "ignored entirely" loop into explicit assertions that they message without costing a turn.
report.evidence:
`npm test` from the project root: 94 tests, 94 pass, 0 fail (exit 0). The new suite covers gold pickup, item pickup with names, the pack cap, the amulet win, potion healing/consumption, equip round trips, equipment-modified damage, dropping, invalid indices, applyKey/runScript and both determinism properties.

Extra manual verification beyond the suite: a scripted dive built only from `applyKey` walked to the stairs and descended from depth 1 to depth 4 on a generated level with seed 5; with an invulnerable bot the same script reached depth 5 (no ">" glyph anywhere, 9 items), walked onto the amulet item sitting on a plain "." tile, and `applyKey(game, "g")` returned ["You found the Amulet of Yendor! You win."] with status "won"; further applyKey calls returned [] and changed nothing. The bot also showed the intended lethality: without cheating it dies at depths 3-4 on seeds 1-12.

Review points: equipment bonuses flow into combat through the real pickup -> use path, not by poking `state.player.equipment` (the skeleton/troll damage numbers in the new test go through the actions); every no-turn path asserted in the suite (wall, nothing here, pack full, invalid use/drop index, unmapped key) leaves `state.turn` unchanged; the two determinism assertions both compare hashes only after asserting `first.state.turn === second.state.turn` (19 on the loot fixture, 8 on the generated seed-99 game) and `reloaded.state.turn === straight.state.turn` (19), so equal hashes cannot come from two runs that did different amounts of work. `git status --short` shows only package.json (pre-existing), src/ and test/; no file outside my scope was touched.
decisions: A valid `use` index always costs a turn, including an unusable item: using the amulet logs "You cannot use the Amulet of Yendor." and advances the turn, because the brief makes only an invalid index free and the design's use bullet ends with "Costs a turn.". `drop` with an invalid index reuses use's "You have no such item." message per the design's "invalid index as above".

runScript returns the concatenation of the non-null message arrays from applyKey (the brief leaves the return value unspecified); whitespace and unknown characters are skipped because applyKey returns null for them. The key table has a null prototype so "toString"/"constructor"/"__proto__" are not keys, and non-string keys return null.

Item names always come from ITEM_KINDS (falling back to the item's own kind string), so a carried item may be a bare { kind } without changing any message. A gold item with no explicit amount contributes 0 instead of poisoning the state with NaN.

The equip-swap branch that drops the displaced item on the floor when the pack is full is unreachable in normal play (splicing the used item out first always frees a slot). It is kept because design section 6.1 specifies it and is covered by a crafted 11-item-pack test.

The potion message reports the hp actually restored, so quaffing at full health says "You quaff the potion and restore 0 hp." — consistent with the design's "restore N hp" while keeping the potion consumed and the turn spent.
One existing test was edited (the "unknown actions" loop) because pickup/use/drop stopped being unknown actions; its new rows assert the messages and the unchanged turn count rather than deletion.
openIssues: A naive beeline bot dies at depths 3-4 on seeds 1-12, so a full five-level dive that ends in the amulet win currently needs either luck or an upgraded player. Not a defect in this task's rules (combat numbers follow the brief), but worth knowing for the integration task and for playability tuning.
