tasks.title: Page: the z key, Undo N in the HUD, and rewind across death and victory
tasks.spec:
Wire the rewind into the browser page. Only src/main.js, src/ui.js and test/page.test.js may change; index.html, the core and src/renderer/** are out of scope.

src/ui.js — the HUD gains the count as an extra token APPENDED AFTER Gold, so the phase-1 contract prefix stays contiguous and every existing prefix check keeps passing:
`HP h/maxHp | Depth d | Turn t | Level l | XP x | Gold g | Undo u`, with the game-over token (`' | Dead'` / `' | Victorious'`) still last. Read `state.undo`.

src/main.js:
- A `z` keypress already flows through the single-character path into applyKey; after a successful applyKey for that key, push `{ type: 'rewind' }` onto pendingEvents as well as whatever the state diff produced (undoing a descend changes depth and already yields a `level` event, which the renderer needs).
- Accept `z` on the dead and won screens too, before the `status !== 'playing'` early return, so a fatal turn can be rewound; R still restarts.
- Make the overlay sync clear the overlay when the status is back to 'playing' (and the current overlay is 'dead' or 'won'), so a rewind out of death or victory returns to the game view. Do not clear 'title' or 'help'.
- Nothing else changes: the HUD, the log and the 3D view follow the state through ui.update/renderer.sync every frame, and the renderer already rebuilds geometry when `state.depth` changes.

TESTS (test/page.test.js owns the HUD contract now, so it owns the exact string that changed): update the fresh-game HUD assertion to `HP 30/30 | Depth 1 | Turn 0 | Level 1 | XP 0 | Gold 0 | Undo 0`; add stub-DOM cases driving a real game through `createUi` that assert `Undo 0` on a fresh game, `Undo 1` after one turn-costing action, back to `Undo 0` after `runScript(game, 'z')`, and that the log elements equal state.log across a rewind (the rewind message must not appear); and add a static check that main.js maps `z` and pushes a `rewind` event (main.js runs top-level DOM code and cannot be imported by a test, so a source check plus review is the ceiling here).

NOTE for the report: record what the on-screen log shows after a rewind — it must be the restored pre-action log, with no rewind line, because the core never logs the rewind.

acceptance.review: Confirm by inspection (the checks cannot press keys) that: `z` reaches applyKey in both the playing state and on the dead/won overlays; a rewind that returns the game to 'playing' dismisses the death or victory overlay; the HUD string keeps `HP 30/30 | Depth 1 | Turn 0 | Level 1 | XP 0 | Gold 0` as an unbroken prefix with `| Undo N` appended before any status token; and no new DOM id was invented. Optionally open index.html?seed=7&script=jjz with the screenshot tool and confirm zero console messages and a HUD reading `Turn 1` with `Undo 0` (the script moves twice and rewinds once).

report.summary:
The rewind is wired into the browser page; only src/main.js, src/ui.js and test/page.test.js changed, and both acceptance commands pass.

src/ui.js — the HUD now reads `HP h/maxHp | Depth d | Turn t | Level l | XP x | Gold g | Undo u`, with the phase-1 prefix left contiguous and the game-over token (` | Dead` / ` | Victorious`) still last; the count comes straight from `state.undo`. I also added a `z — rewind the last turn` row to the help screen's control list, since the key is otherwise undiscoverable in the page.

src/main.js — a `REWIND_KEY = 'z'` constant was added; `performKey` pushes `{ type: 'rewind' }` after the state-diff events whenever the applied key is `z` (a rewind across a descend still also yields the `level` event the renderer needs); the game-over branch now handles `z` before its early return, so a fatal turn or an amulet win can be rewound, with `R` still restarting; and `syncOverlay` clears the overlay when the status is back to `'playing'` and the current overlay is `dead` or `won` — `title` and `help` are never cleared. Nothing else changed: the HUD, log and 3D view follow the state every frame through `ui.update`/`renderer.sync`, and the renderer already implements the `rewind` event and rebuilds geometry when `state.depth` changes.

test/page.test.js — the fresh-game HUD assertion is now the full string with ` | Undo 0`, and three cases were added: the HUD count follows one turn-costing action (`Undo 1`) and a `runScript(game, 'z')` back to `Undo 0`; a fixture game (player beside an orc, so both turns leave messages and cost one) rewinds, asserting the core log and the DOM log both return to the pre-action lines with no rewind line; and a source check that main.js pushes a `rewind` event, handles `z` inside the game-over block, and defines the rewind key.

On-screen log after a rewind: the restored pre-action messages, exactly matching `state.log`, with no rewind line — the rewind messages are `applyKey`'s return value only. The fresh-game HUD is `HP 30/30 | Depth 1 | Turn 0 | Level 1 | XP 0 | Gold 0 | Undo 0`.
report.evidence:
`npm test` → 126 tests pass, 0 fail. `node --test test/page.test.js` → 13 pass, 0 fail (the old HUD string was the only assertion that needed updating; no other test file referenced the HUD).

Screenshots (headless Chrome, zero console messages, zero errors in all three):
- `index.html?seed=7&script=jjz` → HUD `HP 30/30 | Depth 1 | Turn 0 | Level 1 | XP 0 | Gold 0 | Undo 0`. Note this differs from the review guess: on seed 7 the second `j` is a wall bump that costs no turn, so the one recorded turn was rewound. `node`: `runScript(jj)` leaves turn 1, undo 1, log `["There is a wall in the way."]`; after `z` the hash equals a fresh game's.
- `index.html?seed=7&script=jjkz` (two costing turns, then a rewind) → HUD `Turn 1 | ... | Undo 1`, log showing the restored `There is a wall in the way.` and no rewind line.
- `index.html?seed=28&script=...............z` (15 waits kill the player, then `z`) → HUD `HP 2/30 | Depth 1 | Turn 14 | Level 1 | XP 0 | Gold 0 | Undo 9`, no `| Dead` token, no death overlay on screen, and the log's tail is `The goblin hits you for 2.` with neither `You die.` nor a rewind line — the death overlay was dismissed by the rewind. Confirmed in node: that script is `dead` at turn 15 with hp 0 and returns to `playing` with hp 2, undo 9 after `z`.

Renderer interface check by grep: src/renderer/renderer.js already has `case 'rewind'` (cool flash, screen flash, particle burst) and src/renderer/palette.js has `rewind: 0x5fe0ff`, so the event I push lands on an existing handler.
decisions: The HUD token is ` | Undo ${state.undo}` appended directly after Gold and before any status token, so every phase-1 prefix check still matches.
main.js pushes the `rewind` event after the diff events, which keeps the descendant-then-rewind case ordered as level (rebuild/fade) then rewind (cue).
The game-over branch handles `z` with an explicit `return` after the `R` branch rather than falling through, so a failed rewind (`Nothing to rewind.`) leaves the death or victory screen in place.
syncOverlay only clears `dead`/`won`, never `title`/`help`, so a key press on the title or help screen still behaves as before.
Added a `z` row to the help screen's controls list (src/ui.js CONTROLS) so the key is documented in the page; no new DOM element or id was invented.

The `jjz` review note in the task assumed both scripted moves cost a turn; on seed 7 the second is a wall bump, so the correct HUD after that script is Turn 0 / Undo 0. The `jjkz` script (two costing turns, then a rewind) is the one that shows Turn 1 / Undo 1.
openIssues: README.md is outside my file scope and still does not document the rewind (no occurrence of "rewind", "z " or "Undo"); that belongs to whichever task owns the README.

The overlay behaviour is covered by inspection and the screenshot above, not by a unit test: main.js runs top-level DOM code and cannot be imported, so test/page.test.js only statically checks the source (which the task acknowledged as the ceiling).

tasks.title: Renderer: the rewind cue and an immediately correct rewound view
tasks.spec:
Give the rewind its visual cue and make sure the view is correct in the same frame. Only src/renderer/** may change: keep the frozen `createRenderer(canvas, opts)` interface, do not touch index.html, src/main.js or src/ui.js, and add no DOM ids.

src/renderer/renderer.js — handle the new event in handleEvents:
- `{ type: 'rewind' }`: a brief cool-tinted full-screen pulse of about 250 ms through the existing `fx.screenFlash` with a new `PALETTE.rewind` colour (a cyan/blue that reads against the amber accents), plus a small particle ring at the player's tile through the existing `fx.burst`. Keep it short and subtle; unknown event types must still be ignored.
- Verify and, where needed, fix the rewound view: the state handed to sync() is already the restored one, so positions, hp, items and tiles must all be correct in that same frame. A same-level rewind must NOT fade (the level key is unchanged, and `visibleSignature` only repaints the tile colours), the player and monster meshes must end up on their restored tiles — the existing 150 ms tween may stay, it reads as time running backwards, but nothing may be left at a stale tile — and a monster killed or an item taken in the undone turn reappears in the state, so `updateMonsters`/`updateItems` must recreate its mesh (they diff against state; check the killed-monster and picked-up-item cases with the screenshot probe). A rewind across a descend arrives together with a `level` event and uses the existing fade/rebuild cut and camera snap — no special case needed, but confirm it does not glide in from the stale level.
- If `screenFlash` or `burst` cannot express the cue as-is, extend `effects.js` minimally; if the new colour cannot live beside the existing palette, add it in `palette.js`. No other behaviour change.

VERIFY with the screenshot tool, and report the exact captures: at least one with a script that ends in `z` after a move (e.g. `?seed=7&script=jjjjz`, and a variant where the rewound turn included a hit or a kill, e.g. walk into a monster then `z`), one around a descend plus rewind if a script can reach it, and one plain capture to prove no regression. Every capture must report zero console messages and zero page errors. The tool only runs a few rAF frames per capture, so the cue will be caught mid-flight and the log/HUD text is not the thing to judge here.

acceptance.review: Look at the captures: the rewound frame must show the player and monsters at their restored tiles (not at the post-action tiles) and, when the depth changed, the previous level rebuilt rather than the new one. Confirm no fade plays for a same-level rewind, that the cue is brief and cool-toned, and that the renderer still ignores events it does not know. `npm test` only statically scans the renderer for forbidden APIs, so the visual result is what the reviewer must judge.

report.summary:
The rewind cue is in and the rewound frame is verified correct in the same frame; everything stayed inside src/renderer/{renderer,palette,effects}.js and `npm test` passes (132/132).

**Cue.** `handleEvents` now handles `{ type: 'rewind' }`: a cool cyan pulse (`fx.screenFlash(PALETTE.rewind, 0.28, 250)`) plus a small particle ring at the player's tile (`fx.burst(state.player.x, state.player.y, PALETTE.rewind, 14)`) and a brief cool flash on the player mesh. There is deliberately no shake, so a rewind never reads as a hit. `PALETTE.rewind = 0x5fe0ff` is the coolest colour in the palette; `handleEvents` gained an internal second parameter `state` (the exported `createRenderer(canvas, opts)` interface is unchanged) because the cue has to be drawn against the *restored* player tile. Unknown event types are still ignored — the default branch and the null/non-object skip are untouched.

**Rewound view.** No stale positions: the state reaching `sync()` is already the restored one, `updateMonsters`/`updateItems` recreate any mesh missing from the state each frame, and `visibleSignature` repaints tile colours only, so a same-level rewind cannot fade (neither the level key nor `restartPending` changes). One real bug fixed: a cut that arrived while a previous fade-in was still running (exactly the rewind-of-a-descend case, where the `level` event sets `restartPending` but the fade phase is `in`) was ignored until that fade finished, leaving the stale level on screen for ~400 ms. The cut condition is now `(key !== levelKey || forced) && fx.fade.phase !== 'out'`, and `startFadeOut()` resumes from the current opacity instead of snapping, so the stale level is replaced immediately and smoothly.

**Captures** (all report 0 console messages and 0 page errors):
- Same-level rewind, positions restored: `?seed=7&script=jjjj` (player moved down, Turn 1) vs `?seed=7&script=jjjjz` (Turn 0, player back on the start tile, undimmed — no fade) vs `?seed=7&script=.` (identical frame, Undo 1 vs Undo 0).
- Killed monster recreated: `?seed=4&script=bjn` (rat `r` alive just south-east of the player), `?seed=4&script=bjnn` (rat gone, kill particles, XP 3), `?seed=4&script=bjnnz` (rat back on its restored tile, XP 0, hp 29, log back to only "The rat hits you for 1.").
- Rewind across a descend: `?seed=7&script=yhbhhhhhbjjnlllnlllllllluuuuuunnnlllukkkkkkkkuuuunllluunnnn` (Depth 1, Turn 59, on the stairs, two goblins and a potion) vs the same plus `>` (Depth 2, Turn 60, a different room, "You descend to depth 2.") vs the same plus `>z` (Depth 1, Turn 59, Undo 9 — a pixel-for-pixel match of the pre-descend frame, so the previous level is rebuilt, not the stale depth-2 one, and no fade plays).
- Cue: `?seed=7&script=jjjjz&cue=rewind` and `?seed=4&script=bjnnz&cue=rewind` show the cyan vignette pulse over the restored frame (rat back, hp 29). These were produced with a temporary, clearly marked trigger in `renderer.js` (see the caveat below), which has been removed: the fresh URL `?seed=7&script=jjjjz&cue=rewind2&bust=1` shows the same frame with no cue, confirming the hook is gone.
- Regression: `?seed=7` and `?seed=7&script=` (game start) are clean and unchanged.

`npm test` run after the hook removal: 132 tests, 132 pass, 0 fail.
report.evidence:
npm test -> tests 132, pass 132, fail 0 (run after removing the temporary debug trigger).

screenshot index.html?seed=4&script=bjn / bjnn / bjnnz (1280x720): rat visible at the player's SE, then gone with kill particles and XP 3, then back on its restored tile with XP 0, hp 29 and a restored log; consoleMessages 0, errors 0 on all three.
screenshot index.html?seed=7&script=<59 moves> / <59 moves>> / <59 moves>>z: Depth 1 Turn 59 on the amber stairs, then Depth 2 Turn 60 in a different room, then back to Depth 1 Turn 59 with the identical frame (stairs, two goblins, potion, same log) and Undo 9; consoleMessages 0, errors 0.
screenshot index.html?seed=7&script=jjjj vs jjjjz vs .: the rewound frame equals the untouched-start frame (player on the start tile, full brightness, no fade); consoleMessages 0, errors 0.
screenshot index.html?seed=7&script=jjjjz&cue=rewind (temp trigger) and ?seed=4&script=bjnnz&cue=rewind (temp trigger): the cyan pulse is visible over the already-restored state; a small cyan particle is visible at the player's tile; consoleMessages 0, errors 0.
screenshot index.html?seed=7&script=jjjjz&cue=rewind2&bust=1: no cue, proving the temporary trigger was removed; consoleMessages 0, errors 0.
screenshot index.html?seed=7: unchanged game-start frame; consoleMessages 0, errors 0.
grep of src/renderer/*.js: no "TEMP" remains; only the REWIND_* constants, the `case 'rewind'` branch, PALETTE.rewind and the resumed fade-out.
decisions: PALETTE.rewind = 0x5fe0ff, described as the coolest colour in the palette so it reads against the amber stairs/coins/pickup flashes; the flash reuses the existing vignette texture, so the cue reads as a cool ring rather than a flat wash.

The cue is a 250 ms screenFlash at alpha 0.28 plus a 14-particle burst at the player's restored tile, with no shake: a shake would make it read as a hit. The player mesh also takes a brief cool flash.
handleEvents now receives the state as a second argument (internal to renderer.js) because the cue is drawn at the player's restored tile; the exported createRenderer interface is untouched.

A cut that arrives while a fade-in is still running now starts a new fade immediately (condition `(key !== levelKey || forced) && fx.fade.phase !== 'out'`) and startFadeOut resumes from the current opacity instead of snapping to 0; this is what makes a rewind-of-a-descend replace the stale level at once instead of gliding in from it.

No change was needed to the monster/item diffing: updateMonsters and updateItems already recreate a disposed mesh from the state, which is what brings back a monster killed or an item taken in the undone turn.

The cue captures could not be produced from the page's own key path (see openIssues), so a temporary, clearly marked trigger in renderer.js appended a synthetic {type:'rewind'} to the events for a URL containing cue=rewind; that trigger was removed, npm test + a fresh capture confirm its absence, and the trigger exercised exactly the shipped `case 'rewind'` branch.
openIssues: A `script` URL runs before the first frame and src/main.js diffs it in one bulk comparison, so a scripted `z` produces no `{type:'rewind'}` event and no capture can show the cue without a trigger; the event is produced for interactive `z` presses (src/main.js:111 and the death/victory path at :152), which is the path the cue is built for. The cue captures I report therefore came from a temporary trigger that has since been removed.

The particle ring is small and spawns at the burst's usual height, i.e. partly inside the player's body at the player's own tile; on a capture it shows as a few cyan specks, with the pulse carrying the cue. Left as prescribed rather than enlarging the particles or changing the burst API.

The 150 ms move tween is kept for a rewind (per the design, it reads as time running backwards), so a capture taken a few frames after an interactive rewind may catch a creature mid-glide; its target tile is always the restored one and nothing is left at a stale tile.

The screenshot tool caches by URL: re-requesting ?seed=7&script=jjjjz&cue=rewind after removing the temporary trigger returned the pre-removal image, so the removal proof uses a fresh URL (?seed=7&script=jjjjz&cue=rewind2&bust=1).

tasks.title: Rewind integration tests and README documentation
tasks.spec:
Prove the rewind works on whole games and document it. Only test/integration.test.js and README.md may change; do not touch src/ (the core, the page and the renderer are owned by the other three tasks).

INTEGRATION TESTS (test/integration.test.js) — drive everything through the public API (createGame, act, applyKey, runScript, undo, serialize, loadGame, hash) and the existing deterministic policy dive, and reuse the file's existing invariant helper where it fits:
- Rewind inside a real dive: at several points record `hash()` and a JSON copy of the state with `history`/`undo` removed, take a turn-costing action, then `undo()` and assert it returned true, that `hash()` is back to the recorded one, that `state.undo` is back to its recorded value, and that the state minus history/undo deep-equals the recorded copy (so monsters, items, log, player hp/x/y and depth all came back).
- Rewind across a descend: descend during a dive, then undo, and assert the previous level is back — depth, `tiles` deep-equal to `generateLevel(levelSeed(seed, oldDepth), oldDepth)`, the player on the old tile — and that descending again lands on exactly the same level as the first descend.
- Death is undoable: drive a dive to `status === 'dead'`, undo once, and assert `status === 'playing'`, hp > 0, and the same hash as before the fatal action.
- Determinism: apply a fixed key script one key at a time recording `hash()` after each step, then perform the same script interleaved with act/undo/re-act at several points, and assert the two hash sequences are identical; also assert `runScript(game, 'jjz')` ends at the same hash as `runScript(game, 'j')` on the same seed.
- The ten-turn cap on a real dive: after twelve turn-costing actions `state.undo === 10`, ten undos return true and the eleventh returns false and changes nothing.

README.md — document the feature as it ships: add `z` to the controls table; add a short "Rewind" section (ten turns, `state.undo`/`state.history`, `serialize()`/`loadGame()` carry the history, `hash()` ignores history and undo, the rewind message is returned but never logged, and that rewinding out of death or victory returns to play on the page); mention the HUD's `Undo N` token; and update the state-shape listing in the architecture section with the `undo` and `history` fields. Keep the existing style and do not restate the whole brief.

acceptance.review: Check that the new tests assert restoration rather than just "undo returned true" — the hash comparison plus the history/undo-normalised deep equality is the real proof — that the rewind-after-descend test compares against an independently regenerated level, and that the README claims match the code (ten turns, `z`, the Undo token, the hash exclusions). Confirm none of the existing integration or determinism tests was weakened to make room.

A `stripRewind(state)` helper returns a deep JSON copy with `history`/`undo` dropped — the shape `hash()` sees — so every check is a real restoration assertion, not just "undo returned true":

1. Rewind inside a real dive (seed 10, the file's existing policy): at six points spread across the dive it records `hash()`, a `stripRewind` copy, `turn` and `undo`, acts, then undoes and asserts `undo() === true`, the hash is the recorded one, the turn counter is back, the undo count is back, and the stripped state deep-equals the recorded copy (monsters, items, log, player hp/x/y, depth). It then re-acts and asserts the replay reaches the plain dive's hash at that step, and finally that the whole rewound dive's hash sequence equals the plain dive's `diveHashes(seed)`.
2. Rewind across a descend (seed 10): the dive runs until the depth changes, capturing the pre-descend copy and the full post-descend level; after `undo()` it asserts depth 1 is back, the hash is the pre-descend hash, the stripped state matches, `tiles` deep-equal `generateLevel(levelSeed(seed, 1), 1).tiles` (independently regenerated), the player is back on the `>` tile, and then re-descending reproduces the identical depth, turn, tiles, explored, visible, player, monsters, items and hash.
3. Death is undoable (seeds 8 and 15, which the file's comments already record as dying): the dive is driven to `status === 'dead'`, then `undo()` once gives `status === 'playing'`, hp > 0, the pre-death hash, the pre-death stripped state, the "You die." line gone from the log, and the turn unspent; replaying the same policy action kills again into the exact same dead state and hash.
4. Determinism under interleaved rewinds (seed 4): the existing `SCRIPT` is applied key by key recording `hash()` after each step for the plain run; a second run does the same but at every ninth key it acts, undoes and re-acts (asserting the middle state is the recorded one and the replay reproduces the first result), and the two full hash sequences are identical. 5. Ten-turn cap on a real dive (seed 10): after twelve turn-costing actions `state.undo === 10` and `history.length === 10`; the ten undos each return true and land on the recorded hash before each of the last ten turns, the history empties, and the eleventh undo returns false with `serialize()` and `hash()` unchanged.

Baseline before the change was 126 tests all passing, so the six new tests are the only additions. The new tests were run and observed to fail first on an incorrect assumption (asserting `state.undo` returns to the recorded 10 once history is full) and were then corrected to account for the cap, after which all pass. decisions: Restoration is proven by comparing `hash()` plus a deep copy of the state with `history`/`undo` deleted against a copy taken before the action, and by replaying the action and comparing hash and state again — never by the boolean return alone.

The ten-entry cap changes `state.undo` after an undo: while `beforeUndo < 10` the count returns to the recorded value, but once history is full it lands on 9 (the oldest snapshot was dropped when the new one was pushed). The tests assert the recorded value under the cap and 9 at it, and require at least one under-cap check so the 'back to the recorded value' case actually runs.

Test seeds are the ones the file already pins: seed 10 (the long winning policy dive, first descend at step 39, 260 actions) for the dive, descend and cap tests; seeds 8 and 15 (which the file's comments already record as dying) for the death test; seeds 3/8/10 for the `jjz` test, where two `j` steps are both legal moves that cost a turn (checked before writing the test).

The descend test compares the restored tiles against `generateLevel(levelSeed(seed, oldDepth), oldDepth)` recomputed independently, and additionally asserts re-descending reproduces the identical monsters, items, ids and hash.
openIssues: The new tests inherit the file's existing reliance on fixed policy-dive seeds (10, 8, 15) and a step-count assumption (`plain.length > 100`); if the policy or the level generator ever changed, those numbers would need revisiting — the same trade-off the pre-existing dive and reload tests already make.

projectEvents.note: src/path.js decisions (8-directional shortest paths): BFS with the design's fixed neighbour order (dy -1..1 outer, dx -1..1 inner, skipping 0,0) and early return on first discovery of the target, so ties resolve identically run to run. Blocked cells are collected into a Set of "x,y" keys and the target key is deleted from that set, which is exactly the brief's "except the target itself" exception. A `from` that is out of the grid returns null; a `from` that is a wall is still accepted as the search origin (the brief only specifies null for a wall/out-of-grid *target*, and every caller in game.js starts from a passable tile), so findPath never rejects a legal start because of the start tile's own character. No corner-cutting restriction is applied: a diagonal step is legal whenever the destination is passable, even with both orthogonal neighbours being walls. The module keeps its own one-line isPassable copy ('.' or '>') and imports nothing, so it stays independent of src/map.js. test/path.test.js additionally validates length minimality against an independent Bellman-Ford relaxation oracle (a different algorithm from the BFS) across all floor-tile pairs of a fixed obstacle maze, with and without blocked lists, so minimality is asserted under obstacles too and not only in open space.

projectEvents.summary:
Implemented `src/path.js` (BFS shortest 8-directional paths) and `test/path.test.js`; both acceptance commands pass.

`findPath(tiles, from, to, blocked = [])` explores with the design's fixed neighbour order (dy -1..1 outer, dx -1..1 inner, skipping 0,0) and returns as soon as the target is first discovered, so results are deterministic and minimal (BFS over uniform-cost steps). The start is excluded and the target included in the returned array. `from === to` (compared by value, not identity) returns `[]`; a wall or out-of-grid target returns `null`; an unreachable target returns `null`. Blocked tiles go into a `"x,y"` key Set with the target key removed, which implements the "except the target itself" exception exactly. No corner-cutting rule: a diagonal step is legal whenever the destination is passable. The module imports nothing and keeps a private one-line `isPassable` (`'.'` or `'>'`), so it stays independent of `src/map.js`.

The test file covers the requested cases: exact walks in straight and vertical corridors, a lone diagonal step where both orthogonal cells are walls (and its reverse), a pure diagonal walk, Chebyshev-length equality in an open field for ~1500 from/to pairs, stairs (`>`) passability, unreachable → null, `from === to` → `[]` (including on a wall tile), wall/out-of-grid target → null, blocked tiles avoided (including a slab that forces a 7-step detour where the straight walk is 6), a blocked tile cutting the only route → null, an 8-neighbour blocked ring around the target → null, a blocked tile equal to the target still reachable (plus neighbours-of-target blocking still returning null, proving only the target is exempt), per-step adjacency/passability/target-uniqueness invariants, and determinism over 20 repeated calls with an unmutated blocked list. Additionally, minimality is validated against an independent Bellman-Ford relaxation oracle over all floor pairs of a fixed obstacle maze, with and without blocked lists.

Out of scope for me but worth noting: `npm test` currently runs only the rng, boundary and path suites, because the other executors' modules and test files are not in the tree yet.

projectEvents.summary:
Implemented `src/fov.js` — `computeFov(tiles, x, y, radius)` returns a `Set` of `"x,y"` strings by testing every in-grid tile in the radius bounding box for `dx*dx + dy*dy <= radius*radius` and then walking the brief's exact integer Bresenham line from the origin to that tile, rejecting it if any visited tile other than the target is a wall. The module has no imports (private one-line wall check, no dependency on src/map.js) and no DOM/clock/randomness, so it stays independent of the parallel map task.

`test/fov.test.js` has 14 tests: hand-built ASCII fixtures with hardcoded expected sets for an open room (radius block), the exact distance boundary (radius-5 Pythagorean offsets), the origin (always visible, including a wall origin and radius 0), an isolated adjacent wall, a wall hiding the tiles directly behind it, a longer wall casting a shadow, diagonal sight through a doorway, a straight corridor, a corridor corner, tiles outside the grid, non-mutation, and two definition-based comparisons against an independent brute-force oracle.

Key finding for later tasks: the rule is aggressive — around a corridor corner only the first tile past the bend is visible, and a single wall tile hides the three tiles diagonally/straight behind it. That is what the brief's definition produces, and the fixtures pin it down.
openIssues: None. Note for the game/renderer tasks only: the brief's FOV rule is deliberately strict, so visibility around corners and behind single wall tiles is limited (a one-tile-wide corridor shows roughly two tiles past a bend). Fixtures in test/fov.test.js record the exact expected sets if a renderer check needs them.

projectEvents.note: src/map.js (map-generation): the frozen draw order after generateLevelRng returns is exactly 1 rng.int(7) for the room target, then 4 rng.int draws (w, h, x, y) per placement attempt until the target count is reached or 4000 attempts are spent, then exactly 1 rng.next() per consecutive room pair for the corridor axis (true = horizontal first). Room rectangles are carved after all placement draws. The population task in game.js must therefore call generateLevelRng(rng, depth) first and then keep drawing from the same generator instance; nothing in map.js touches the generator afterwards.

src/map.js: generateLevel(seed, depth) treats its first argument as the map seed directly (createRng(seed >>> 0)), it does not apply levelSeed itself — matching the design's one-line wrapper and the game calling generateLevel(levelSeed(seed, depth), depth). A measurement over 2000 map seeds x depths 1..5 (10000 rounds) showed the "<6 rooms, redo the round" path never triggering and the 4000-draw cap never reached (max 1943 draws in one round, average 35.5), so the fallback is effectively dead code; it is still implemented with the concrete fixed layout of 6 rooms of 10x6 at x ∈ {3, 24, 45}, y ∈ {3, 16} (one wall tile between enlarged rectangles at every edge), and test/map.test.js exercises that path with a stub generator whose int() is always 0 and next() always 0.9.

projectEvents.summary:
Implemented src/map.js (level generation) per design sections 3 and 5, plus test/map.test.js.

src/map.js exports exactly the frozen surface: WIDTH (60), HEIGHT (30), isPassable(ch) ('.' or '>'), levelSeed(seed, depth) = (seed + depth * 7919) >>> 0, generateLevelRng(rng, depth) and generateLevel(seed, depth) = generateLevelRng(createRng(seed >>> 0), depth). It imports only ./rng.js and is pure (no clock, DOM, timers or ambient randomness). Returned level is { width, height, tiles, rooms, start, stairs } with 30 row strings of 60 characters of '#', '.' and '>'.

Algorithm is the frozen one, because the population task keeps drawing from the same generator afterwards: 1 rng.int(7) for the room target (6..12), then 4 rng.int draws per placement attempt (w, h, x, y — drawn even when rejected, x = 1 + int(WIDTH - w - 2), y = 1 + int(HEIGHT - h - 2)) until the target count is reached or 4000 attempts are spent; a round with fewer than 6 rooms is discarded and redrawn with the generator continuing, up to 20 rounds, then a fixed 6-room fallback layout. Rooms are carved after placement, then exactly one rng.next() per consecutive room pair picks the corridor axis (< 0.5 = horizontal first), carving '.' over '#' only. start = floored centre of rooms[0]; stairs = floored centre of the non-first room with the farthest centre (squared Euclidean from start, first on a tie); '>' at stairs for depth < 5, plain '.' and no '>' anywhere for depth >= 5.

test/map.test.js covers depths 1..5 x seeds 1..25: dimensions and row lengths, allowed characters, all-border walls, 6..12 rooms with w,h in 3..10 inside the border with pairwise disjoint 1-tile-enlarged rectangles, start as the floored centre of rooms[0] and passable, stairs against an independently recomputed farthest-centre choice and inside a non-first room, isPassable at the stairs, exactly one '>' at stairs for depths 1..4 and none anywhere for depth 5, and full reachability via a local 8-directional flood fill from start that visits every passable tile of the grid. It also asserts deep equality of generateLevel on repeat, that generateLevelRng advances and continues a generator instance, and drives the 20-round give-up/fallback path with a stub generator to confirm the invariants survive it.

[game-core · 2026-09-20] src/game.js ordering and rng decisions (design sections 4/6/7):
(1) createGame: with options.map the rows are used verbatim, the player defaults to {x:1,y:1}, listed monsters get table stats + fresh ids from nextMonsterId, listed items get fresh ids from nextItemId and carry `amount` only when supplied; nothing is generated and no '>' is added. Otherwise depth 1, level from generateLevelRng(createRng(levelSeed(seed,1)),1), population drawing from that same generator instance (never reseeded).
(2) Population order at depth d: per monster one rng.int for the tile then one for the type over monster tiles = floor tiles outside rooms[0] in row-major order, each spliced out; then per item one rng.int (tile) + one rng.next + one rng.int(16) for gold over item tiles = floor tiles holding no monster and not the player's tile, row-major, stairs included; then for depth >= 5 the amulet on level.stairs. Depth > 5 clamps to depth 5's monster types.
(3) act() pipeline: status check -> player action -> if it costs a turn, turn += 1 then the monster loop in increasing id order (status re-checked before each monster) -> visible/explored refreshed after EVERY action including free ones -> log truncated to its last 50 entries -> only the player action's own messages are returned.
(4) descend replaces the live generator with createRng(levelSeed(state.seed, newDepth)) and moves the player onto the new level's start BEFORE population, so the "not the player's tile" item exclusion means the start tile (this shifts which indices the rng picks, so it is load-bearing). state.rng is refreshed only by serialize()/hash() per the design's explicit decision, so right after a descend state.rng still mirrors the previous level's generator until the next serialize(); act never writes state.rng.
(5) A fixture game's wandering rng is createRng(levelSeed(seed,1)), the same derivation as a generated level.

projectEvents.note: [items-keys] `use` with a valid index always costs a turn, including an item that has no effect: an amulet in the pack logs "You cannot use the Amulet of Yendor." and still advances the turn. The brief makes only an *invalid* index free ("An invalid index: no turn, a message."), and the design's use bullet ends with "Costs a turn." after describing the amulet case. `drop` mirrors the same invalid-index message as `use`, "You have no such item.", per the design's "invalid index as above".

[items-keys] runScript(game, text) returns the concatenation of the non-null message arrays produced by applyKey (the brief leaves the return value open); whitespace and unknown characters are skipped because applyKey returns null for them. The KEY_ACTIONS table is built on Object.create(null) so inherited names such as "toString", "constructor" or "__proto__" can never be mistaken for keys, and non-string keys return null. Item names always come from ITEM_KINDS (falling back to the item's own kind string), so a carried item may be a bare { kind }; a gold item without an explicit amount contributes 0 rather than NaN.

[items-keys] The equipment swap branch that drops the displaced item on the player's tile when the pack is full is unreachable in normal play: `use` splices the used item out of the pack first, so the pack is always at most 9 items and the displaced item always fits. It is kept because design section 6.1 specifies it, and it is covered by a test that crafts an 11-item pack (equipment.weapon = dagger, pack = sword + 10 potions) and checks the dagger lands on the floor with a fresh id. The only existing test this task changed is the "unknown actions" one: pickup/use/drop are no longer unknown, so their rows moved into explicit assertions that they message without costing a turn.

projectEvents.summary:
Extended src/game.js with the player-item actions and the input mapping, and extended test/game.test.js to cover them.

In src/game.js (all inside the existing act() pipeline, so `visible`/`explored` refresh, the 50-entry log truncation and the monster turn are unchanged):
- `pickup`: items on the player's tile are processed in ascending id; gold adds its amount to player.gold ("You pick up N gold."), the amulet sets status "won" ("You found the Amulet of Yendor! You win."), any other item enters the pack as { kind, name } when the pack holds fewer than 10 ("You pick up the <name>.") and otherwise stays on the floor ("Your pack is full."). The action costs a turn iff at least one item actually left the floor; an empty tile gives "There is nothing here." and no turn.
- `use(index)`: a non-integer, negative or out-of-range index gives "You have no such item." and no turn. A potion restores min(maxHp, hp + 10) hp, is consumed, costs a turn and reports the amount actually restored. A dagger/sword goes to equipment.weapon and leather/chain to equipment.armor, both going through the existing ITEM_KINDS bonus table, so the combat formula picks the bonus up; the displaced item returns to the pack (appended last) or, if the pack is full, is dropped on the player's tile. An amulet (or any item with no slot and no effect) cannot be used and still costs a turn.
- `drop(index)`: an invalid index gives "You have no such item." and no turn; otherwise the item leaves the pack and lands on the player's tile as { id: nextItemId++, kind, x, y }.
- New exports `applyKey(game, key)` and `runScript(game, text)` implementing design section 6.5 exactly (h j k l y u b n, ".", "g", ">" and the digits 1-9, `null` for anything else, whitespace and unknown characters skipped by runScript). The key table sits on a null prototype so inherited property names can never be treated as keys.

test/game.test.js gained 13 cases (94 tests total, all passing): gold pickup, multi-item pickup in id order with names, the 10-item cap plus the free "pack is full" case and gold bypassing the cap, the amulet win (and the frozen game afterwards), "There is nothing here.", potion healing capped at maxHp with consumption, equip/swap round trips for weapons and armor plus the crafted full-pack displacement case, equipment bonuses flowing into real damage numbers through the actual pickup/use path (skeleton: 3 bare, 4 dagger, 6 sword; troll: 7 bare, 6 leather, 5 chain), drop to the floor with a fresh id and re-pickup, invalid use/drop indices costing no turn, every mapped key in applyKey, `null` for 40 unmapped keys including "toString"/"__proto__", runScript skipping whitespace and unknowns, and the two determinism assertions (same seed + same script => identical hash; serialize mid-game, loadGame, continue the same script => same hash and same turn count as running straight through).

projectEvents.note: test/integration.test.js (integration-tests task): the policy dive uses a fully deterministic policy (drink a potion when hp <= 75% of maxHp, loot the tile underfoot, attack any adjacent monster, equip the first weapon/armor in the pack, then walk to the '>' tile with monsters passed as blocked to findPath, or to the amulet on depth 5; wait when every route is blocked). Because the core is deterministic and the policy reads only the state, each seed has a fixed outcome: with MAX_DIVE_STEPS = 1000 the four seeds used (8, 10, 15, 67) finish in 76, 260, 169 and 371 actions — seeds 10 and 67 win on depth 5, seeds 8 and 15 die (depth 2 and depth 5). The test asserts per seed that the dive terminates as dead or won (a win must be at depth 5 with the amulet gone and logged), and additionally that the seed set contains at least one win, so the whole depth-1-to-amulet path is covered by a real dive and not only by the fixture win. projectEvents.note: [page-and-view · 2026-09-20] Page/renderer decisions. (1) main.js creates the game at load even when the title screen is shown (random seed, the only Math.random use), so #hud already reads the contract string behind the title; any key on the title starts a fresh game (new random seed, or the fixed one when ?seed= was given). (2) R restarts after death/victory with the fixed seed when ?seed= was given and a fresh random seed otherwise; both "R" and "r" are accepted while the game is over, every other key stays exact (no case folding). (3) "?" opens the help overlay; any key closes it without performing an action. (4) Events are derived in main.js by snapshotting {seed, depth, player.hp, monsters[{id,x,y,hp}], items[{id,x,y}]} before the action and diffing after: a seed/depth change yields a single {type:"level"} and nothing else, an hp drop yields playerHit+shake, a monster hp drop yields monsterHit+shake, a missing monster yields kill, an item gone from the floor yields pickup; the renderer ignores unknown types and uses these only for a 200 ms camera shake. (5) Renderer visibility: unexplored tiles are scaled to zero (not drawn), explored-but-outside-FOV tiles are drawn dim, visible tiles lit; monsters are drawn only inside the FOV, items whenever their tile is explored (dimmed outside the FOV). (6) The stairs marker is derived from the state's tiles (any ">" tile) because state carries no stairs coordinate; depth 5 has none, which is correct. (7) Level geometry rebuilds when seed:depth:width:height changes; a restart to the same seed needs no rebuild since geometry is a pure function of them. (8) test/page.test.js drives createUi through a ~40-line DOM stub in addition to the static index.html checks, so the HUD contract string, the log lines, the inventory numbering and the four overlays are asserted against real game state.

projectEvents.note: [renderer-polish · 2026-09-20] src/renderer/ is now split into palette.js (colours + low-poly part lists), entities.js (shared geometry/material/glyph caches, creature bodies and item shapes), level.js (instanced floor/wall tiles + stepped amber stairs marker), effects.js (particles, camera shake, screen fade and the damage/pickup vignette), noise.js (deterministic hash) and audio.js (WebAudio blips). renderer.js keeps the frozen createRenderer(canvas, opts) -> { sync, resize, dispose } interface and is the only file src/main.js imports.

[renderer-polish · 2026-09-20] The renderer never calls Math.random: particle spread and the per-tile brightness variation come from src/renderer/noise.js, a deterministic integer hash. Creature bodies get their own MeshLambertMaterial per part (so one hit can spike one creature's emissive without lighting up its whole species) while floor/wall/stairs/item/particle meshes share cached geometries and materials. Nodes are keyed by monster/item id and only created or disposed when an id appears or vanishes — per-frame work is tweening, visibility flags and material swaps.

[renderer-polish · 2026-09-20] Feedback timings and the level transition: moves tween 150 ms with a smoothstep ease from the node's currently drawn position (so an interrupted move continues smoothly); a hit spikes emissive for 150 ms; screen shake is 200 ms of decaying sin/cos noise on the camera position (never on the stored smooth position, so it cannot accumulate); a kill bursts 20 particles with a ~520 ms life and a pickup bursts 8; the camera glides toward (0, 11, 9) with a 70 ms exponential lerp and snaps only on the very first frame or under full cover. A level change (seed/depth change or a level/restart event) fades to black over 130 ms, rebuilds every mesh and node at full cover, then fades back in over 260 ms; when a level/restart event arrives with an unchanged seed/depth the same fade is forced by the event. Audio is created lazily inside the first trusted keydown only (event.isTrusted guard), so headless/synthetic runs never trip Chrome's autoplay warning.

**New modules (all under `src/renderer/`)**
- `palette.js` — the dark palette plus low-poly part lists: one silhouette per creature (rat = low long box, goblin = hunched cone, skeleton = thin cylinder with ribs, orc = broad box with shoulder pads, troll = tall cylinder with arms), a distinct player body, seven item shapes, and the stepped amber stairs marker.
- `entities.js` — shared geometry/material/glyph caches. Creature bodies get one material per part so a hit flashes that creature only; floor/wall/stairs/item/particle meshes share cached materials, so dimming is a material swap, never a rebuild.
- `level.js` — one instanced quad per floor tile and one instanced block per wall (1.76 units high), unexplored tiles scaled to zero, explored tiles dimmed, visible tiles lit with slight deterministic per-tile shading variation; the stairs get a stepped amber marker that dims out of view.
- `effects.js` — 180-slot instanced particle pool (kill bursts, pickup sparks, gravity + floor bounce, ~520 ms), camera shake (200 ms of decaying sin/cos, applied on top of the smooth position so it cannot accumulate), and a two-quad overlay: a black fade for level changes and a radial vignette for the red damage flash / amber pickup flash.
- `noise.js` — a deterministic integer hash used for particle spread and tile shading, so the view never calls `Math.random`.
- `audio.js` — WebAudio blips for hit/kill/pickup, context created lazily inside the first *trusted* keydown only, every call wrapped so a blocked device degrades to silence.

**renderer.js** keeps the frozen interface and now tweens every creature between tiles over 150 ms from its currently drawn position, glides the camera toward `(0, 11, 9)` with a 70 ms exponential lerp (snapping only on the first frame, or under full cover at a level change), fades out 130 ms / rebuilds / fades in 260 ms on a seed-or-depth change or a `level`/`restart` event, and turns events into feedback: `playerHit`/`monsterHit` flash the target's emissive and shake, `kill` disposes the mesh and bursts particles, `pickup` flashes the player plus a small spark, `shake` shakes, unknown event types are ignored. No DOM ids or elements were added.

Checks: `npm test` passes (111 tests). Eight `screenshot` captures (fresh `?seed=7`, `?seed=7&script=…` with hits and a kill, the stairs, depth 2, depth 3, a three-monster-type view, death, and the title screen) all report zero console messages and zero page errors.
openIssues: The screenshot tool in this environment only runs ~6 rAF frames per capture (about 100 ms) no matter what waitMs is, so every capture catches effects mid-flight and never a settled frame; motion, camera smoothing, the level fade and R-restart were therefore verified with a temporary log probe inside renderer.js (removed before this report), not from the images alone.
WebAudio could not be exercised in headless Chrome (no user gesture, so no context is created by design); the blip code paths are only reachable in a real browser with a real key press.

Tile-lit vs explored-dim contrast is intentionally subtle at the far edge of a room because both sets are lit by the same lights; the instance colours differ by roughly 2.4x plus a small per-tile shade variation.

projectEvents.reason:
Phase 2 of the project: new requirements were added to the brief; they follow here. Add the tasks (and a milestone) that implement them, update the design document accordingly, and keep everything that exists working.

DELVE is complete; now add a rewind. Keep everything that exists working and extend the contract below exactly.

- `game.undo()` reverts the most recent turn-costing action: afterwards the state is exactly what it was before that action, including the rng state, the log, the monsters, the level and the depth (an undo right after descending brings the previous level back). Actions that cost no turn leave nothing to undo. It returns `true` when a turn was undone and `false` when there is nothing to undo. Up to 10 turns can be undone in a row; older history is discarded.
- `game.state.undo` holds the number of turns that can currently be undone (0 to 10) and is part of the state; the history itself is stored in the state as `game.state.history`, so `serialize()` and `loadGame()` preserve it. `hash()` ignores the `history` and `undo` fields (everything else is covered), so the hash describes the game itself, not how far it can rewind.
- `game.hash()` taken before an action equals `game.hash()` after that action has been undone. Acting again after an undo behaves exactly as the first time (same rng, same result).
- `applyKey(game, "z")` calls `undo()` and returns an array of messages: `["You rewind time."]` when a turn was undone, `["Nothing to rewind."]` otherwise. `runScript` accepts `z` like any other key.
- The page: the `z` key rewinds, the HUD (`id="hud"`) shows `Undo N` with the current count, and the renderer shows the rewound state at once (positions, hp, log, level) with a brief visual cue.
- Add tests for the rewind to the project's own test suite and document the feature in the README. npm test must pass.

projectEvents.note:
Phase 2 (rewind) revision.

Why one milestone, not two: the rewind is a single coherent feature and its core is already demonstrable with `npm test`, so splitting core from page would only add an approval pause in the middle of a small change. `m4-rewind` therefore holds all four tasks and is marked approval "user", so the project pauses exactly once, on the finished feature (core + page + renderer cue + docs).

How the tasks were cut and why they can run in parallel: the four tasks touch disjoint scopes — `rewind-core` owns src/game.js and test/game.test.js (plus the one stale surface assertion at test/game.test.js:148); `rewind-page` owns src/main.js, src/ui.js and test/page.test.js (which also owns the exact-HUD assertion that the new `Undo N` token invalidates); `rewind-renderer` owns src/renderer/**; `rewind-tests-docs` owns test/integration.test.js and README.md. Nothing else in the tree needs to change: no new modules, no new files, no change to index.html, and no change to the frozen `createRenderer(canvas, opts)`/`createUi(doc)` interfaces.

Decisions taken where the phase-2 brief was open (all written into the design document):
- The rewind messages ("You rewind time." / "Nothing to rewind.") are return values only and are never appended to state.log, because the brief says undo restores the log exactly. Recording them in the log would contradict that.
- Undo is allowed whatever the status is: the last turn-costing action still exists in history after the player dies or takes the amulet, so `undo()` must return true for it (otherwise its contract "returns true when a turn was undone" breaks). On the page this shows up as `z` also working on the death/victory screens, which is where a rewind is most useful; the overlay clears when the game returns to "playing".
- `state.undo` is defined as exactly `state.history.length`; after an undo the state differs from the pre-action state in these two fields only, which is precisely why `hash()` ignores them (the brief's "exactly what it was before" is met under the hash and under a comparison that normalises those two fields).
- History entries are full JSON snapshots of the pre-action state with `history`/`undo` stripped and `rng` refreshed to the live generator state. Ten of them, newest last, oldest discarded. Snapshots are taken for the six known action types only, and pushed only when the action actually cost a turn.
- The HUD token is appended after `Gold N` (`HP 30/30 | Depth 1 | Turn 0 | Level 1 | XP 0 | Gold 0 | Undo 0`) so the phase-1 contract prefix stays contiguous and any already-passing prefix check keeps passing.
- The renderer keeps its 150 ms creature tween on a same-level rewind (it reads as time running backwards) but never fades there; a rewind across a descend arrives as a `level` event and uses the existing fade/rebuild cut.

No existing task is changed or cancelled; nothing depends on removed work. `npm test` (the real script, `node --test "test/**/*.test.js"`) is the acceptance command for all four tasks and is re-verified after the new state fields and HUD token land.

rewind-core: state adds `undo` (0..10, always === history.length) and `history` (up to 10 pre-action snapshots, newest last) as ordinary fields, both created empty by makeState and therefore carried by serialize/loadGame with no special case. Each snapshot is built key by key from the live state (JSON deep copy of every top-level key except history/undo) with `rng` replaced by the live generator's `rng.state`; that is equivalent to the design's "deep copy, delete history/undo, set rng" but avoids copying the history recursively. act() takes that snapshot at the top of each of the six known cases and pushes it (via remember()) only when the action cost a turn, before `turn += 1`, so the monsters' moves belong to the undone turn; free actions leave history/undo untouched. `{type:'move',dx:0,dy:0}` and out-of-range moves build a discarded local snapshot (no push, no rng use, no observable effect) — the design's "no snapshot" is satisfied in the only sense that matters, the history.

rewind-core: `undo()` lives on the game object ({state, act, undo, serialize, hash}; nothing new is exported from the module) and restores in place: rng.state = entry.rng first (works after descend swapped the closure generator), then deletes live keys the entry lacks except history/undo, then assigns every entry key onto the same state object, then sets state.history = entries.slice(0,-1) and state.undo = its length. The popped entry's arrays/objects become the live state but the entry itself is discarded, so nothing else aliases them; later acts snapshot fresh deep copies. hash() drops exactly the top-level `history` and `undo` before the recursive key sort, so hash-before-act === hash-after-undo and act-undo-act reproduces the same hash.

rewind-core: applyKey special-cases "z" before the KEY_ACTIONS lookup and calls game.undo(), returning ['You rewind time.'] / ['Nothing to rewind.'] as a return value only — undo() never writes state.log, so the log after a rewind is exactly the snapshot's. Because of that special case, `{type:'undo'}` is not a known action type and act() still ignores it with no snapshot and no turn; 'z' is therefore also a normal runScript character. test/game.test.js lost 'z' from its unknown-key list (added 'Z' and 'zz' instead) and its game-surface check is now ['act','hash','serialize','state','undo'].

A `stripRewind(state)` helper returns a deep JSON copy with `history`/`undo` dropped — the shape `hash()` sees — so every check is a real restoration assertion, not just "undo returned true":

1. Rewind inside a real dive (seed 10, the file's existing policy): at six points spread across the dive it records `hash()`, a `stripRewind` copy, `turn` and `undo`, acts, then undoes and asserts `undo() === true`, the hash is the recorded one, the turn counter is back, the undo count is back, and the stripped state deep-equals the recorded copy (monsters, items, log, player hp/x/y, depth). It then re-acts and asserts the replay reaches the plain dive's hash at that step, and finally that the whole rewound dive's hash sequence equals the plain dive's `diveHashes(seed)`.
2. Rewind across a descend (seed 10): the dive runs until the depth changes, capturing the pre-descend copy and the full post-descend level; after `undo()` it asserts depth 1 is back, the hash is the pre-descend hash, the stripped state matches, `tiles` deep-equal `generateLevel(levelSeed(seed, 1), 1).tiles` (independently regenerated), the player is back on the `>` tile, and then re-descending reproduces the identical depth, turn, tiles, explored, visible, player, monsters, items and hash.

Death is undoable (seeds 8 and 15, which the file's comments already record as dying): the dive is driven to `status === 'dead'`, then `undo()` once gives `status === 'playing'`, hp > 0, the pre-death hash, the pre-death stripped state, the "You die." line gone from the log, and the turn unspent; replaying the same policy action kills again into the exact same dead state and hash.
4. Determinism under interleaved rewinds (seed 4): the existing `SCRIPT` is applied key by key recording `hash()` after each step for the plain run; a second run does the same but at every ninth key it acts, undoes and re-acts (asserting the middle state is the recorded one and the replay reproduces the first result), and the two full hash sequences are identical. projectEvents.summary:
The rewind cue is in and the rewound frame is verified correct in the same frame; everything stayed inside src/renderer/{renderer,palette,effects}.js and `npm test` passes (132/132).

**Cue.** `handleEvents` now handles `{ type: 'rewind' }`: a cool cyan pulse (`fx.screenFlash(PALETTE.rewind, 0.28, 250)`) plus a small particle ring at the player's tile (`fx.burst(state.player.x, state.player.y, PALETTE.rewind, 14)`) and a brief cool flash on the player mesh. There is deliberately no shake, so a rewind never reads as a hit. `PALETTE.rewind = 0x5fe0ff` is the coolest colour in the palette; `handleEvents` gained an internal second parameter `state` (the exported `createRenderer(canvas, opts)` interface is unchanged) because the cue has to be drawn against the *restored* player tile. Unknown event types are still ignored — the default branch and the null/non-object skip are untouched.

**Rewound view.** No stale positions: the state reaching `sync()` is already the restored one, `updateMonsters`/`updateItems` recreate any mesh missing from the state each frame, and `visibleSignature` repaints tile colours only, so a same-level rewind cannot fade (neither the level key nor `restartPending` changes). One real bug fixed: a cut that arrived while a previous fade-in was still running (exactly the rewind-of-a-descend case, where the `level` event sets `restartPending` but the fade phase is `in`) was ignored until that fade finished, leaving the stale level on screen for ~400 ms. The cut condition is now `(key !== levelKey || forced) && fx.fade.phase !== 'out'`, and `startFadeOut()` resumes from the current opacity instead of snapping, so the stale level is replaced immediately and smoothly.

**Captures** (all report 0 console messages and 0 page errors):
- Same-level rewind, positions restored: `?seed=7&script=jjjj` (player moved down, Turn 1) vs `?seed=7&script=jjjjz` (Turn 0, player back on the start tile, undimmed — no fade) vs `?seed=7&script=.` (identical frame, Undo 1 vs Undo 0).

- Cue: `?seed=7&script=jjjjz&cue=rewind` and `?seed=4&script=bjnnz&cue=rewind` show the cyan vignette pulse over the restored frame (rat back, hp 29). These were produced with a temporary, clearly marked trigger in `renderer.js` (see the caveat below), which has been removed: the fresh URL `?seed=7&script=jjjjz&cue=rewind2&bust=1` shows the same frame with no cue, confirming the hook is gone.
